issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This follow-up to PR #6841 tests the best review-ranked ways to make source-push expert-parallel MoE competitive on EP8 H100s. The useful path is the staged semantic implementation: round 1 kept the bf16 `dy` cast, adopted XLA gather-sum combine, and confirmed host-side planning is the largest structural blocker, while owner-sharded `dx` return and fused W13 zero-fill fixes were falsified. The apparent W2-return regression was later traced to the deliberate W2-from-H boundary switch, not branch drift; SPF-008 recovered part of that cost by moving route scaling to the output side (w2_return 7.08 -> 6.36 ms), but naive double-buffering hurt occupancy. Current recommendation: continue on staged semantic/device-sided planning and occupancy-neutral W2-from-H overlap; keep the fused persistent-kernel path quarantined until it passes an integrated numerical gate.

### Helpful links
- PR #6841: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6841
- Round-1 results: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7276#issuecomment-4997344962
- SPF-007 root-cause note: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7276#issuecomment-4999175606
- SPF-008 result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7276#issuecomment-5005358579
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Builds on #6597 / #6848 / PR #6841 at head `26711f86e`, target shape EP8 H100, 32768 tok/rank, top-k 4, 32 experts/rank, d2560/f1280, goal 250 useful TFLOP/s/rank fwd+bwd. Branch: `research/mcwitt/6841-source-push-followup`.

Ranked avenues (gain / effort):

1. `SPF-001` bf16-cast `dy` before the replicated reshard (`source_push_semantic_mlp.py:586`): all-gather payload 2.35 -> 1.17 GB, est. ~5.8 ms off the 63.0 ms API. S.
2. `SPF-002` switch dx return to the existing owner-sharded `psum_scatter` wrapper (`source_push_semantic_mlp.py:621`): all-reduce 4.70 -> 2.35 GB/rank, est. 3-6 ms. S.
3. `SPF-003a` measure unlogged tip commit `26711f86e` (grouped W13 raw gathers) vs the 23.025 ms fused-W13 baseline. Free.
4. `SPF-003b` fused W13-bwd unconditionally remote-writes a zero tile then overwrites it (`source_push_semantic_fused_w13_backward.py:1040`): 2x NVLink bytes on dX return, est. 2-4 ms of 135.5. S.
5. `SPF-004` combine kernel runs at ~21% of HBM roofline (per-row scalar loads, `source_push_combine.py:145`): 1.34 -> ~0.5 ms. S.
6. `SPF-005` host-side numpy planner cost at target shape is excluded from every benchmark number (O(268M) element ops/plan, `source_push_plan.py:636`): measure it. S, CPU-only.
7. Source-push dy route (fix dcombine in_specs `source_push_semantic_backward_pallas.py:2280`, reuse existing dy-route remote-write kernel + global phase barrier): rest of the 11.6 ms API tax. M-L.
8. W2-return kernel double-buffering + deferred `wait_smem_to_gmem` (`source_push_w2_return.py:680-765`): 4.05 -> ~2.7 ms. M.
9. Correctness cluster: single-jit remote-write completion barrier is scalar-only (`source_push_forward.py:1109`); fused dX-return has no wait on `ready_sem` before the combine kernel; integrated numerical gate FUSED-MOE-094 failed (y max-abs-diff 1024) and was never re-cleared. S-M, blocking for fused promotion.
10. SM-carveout restructure (persistent SM-capped comm kernels + pipelined near-stock GEMM consumers; de-fuse W2-return/combine as a dense fixed-shape permute): only credible route to 250. L, design first.

## Hypothesis or Goal

The S-effort tier (1+2+5) takes the honest API from 63.0 to ~50-52 ms (~150 useful) with grad parity, converging on the 44.2 ms manual bound; measurements 3/6 decide where the next M/L unit of work goes.

## Status

Round 1 complete (2026-07-16): SPF-001 keep (-1.87 ms, API 61.008 ms / 126.79 useful), SPF-002 falsified (VJP sharding contract), SPF-003a real but modest (-1.11%), SPF-003b falsified, SPF-004 adopt (XLA combine, bitwise-identical, 1745 GB/s) + W2 hoist keep, SPF-005 confirmed ~190x (380 ms/plan; ~1.85 s public path). New open items: SPF-006 compare-gate regression bisect. SPF-007 resolved from records (no bisect needed): the w2_return 4.05->7.08 ms jump is the deliberate W2-from-H boundary switch (`ae1c9aed1`+`e8fbfa85e`, 2026-07-03), measured contemporaneously; reclassified as avenue-8 kernel work. See round-1 comment and SPF-007 comment. SPF-008 (2026-07-17): avenue 8 executed on branch `spf/008-w2-from-h-kernel` — output-side route scaling ADOPTED (w2_return 7.077 -> 6.355 ms, total 16.72 -> 15.97; numerics bit-match the pre-change smoke; no new pytest failures vs head), 2-stage double-buffering FALSIFIED (8.57 ms: 2x SMEM halves CTA occupancy) and reverted; ~1.4 ms to the ~5.0 ms from_h floor remains, needs an occupancy-neutral overlap design. See SPF-008 comment. 2026-07-17: thread refocused on B200 (production priority) — continues in #7333 (SPB series); this issue is the H100 phase (retitled). Remaining H100 items (SPF-006 compare-gate bisect, occupancy-neutral W2-from-H overlap) deprioritized pending the SPB-001 gate.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/6841-source-push-followup.md` on `research/mcwitt/6841-source-push-followup`
* Prior logbooks: `.agents/logbooks/6597-moe-mgpu-forward.md`, `.agents/logbooks/6597-moe-fused-comm-tensorcore.md`
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

* 2026-07-17: refocus on B200 — production priority; B200 phase opened as #7333 (SPB series); this issue scoped to H100.
* 2026-07-16: perf spend goes to the staged semantic path; fused path gets free measurements + S-effort fixes only until it passes a finite integrated numerical gate.
* 2026-07-16: adopt XLA gather-sum combine (bitwise-identical, faster, deletes a kernel); keep bf16-dy cast and W2 weight-copy hoist; discard zero-fill fix and owner-sharded dx return.
* 2026-07-16: production viability of the public source-push API is gated on device-siding the planner (SPF-005) before any further kernel tuning; next perf unit of work is the SPF-007 bisect.
* 2026-07-17: SPF-008 — adopt output-side route scaling on the W2-from-H kernels (branch `spf/008-w2-from-h-kernel`, `aa38972c8`; -0.72 ms w2_return); reject naive double-buffering for these Lane kernels — overlap designs must keep SMEM under ~112 KB/CTA to preserve 2 CTAs/SM.
* 2026-07-16: SPF-007 closed without a bisect — root cause identified from the 6597 logbook records (W2-from-H switch is a priced-in H-boundary cost, head is +0.03 ms over the day-one 7.048 ms measurement); the recovery path is avenue 8 (output-side route scaling + double-buffered k-loop, ~4.5-5 ms target vs 6.80 ms post-hoist).

## Conclusion

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 SPF round 1 complete — all five experiments ran; results below (logbook has exact commands/jobs; branch `research/mcwitt/6841-source-push-followup` + `spf/00*` experiment branches).

| ID | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| SPF-001 bf16 dy before the replicated reshard | API fwd+bwd 62.876 -> **61.008 ms** (126.79 useful), grad parity within accepted threshold | Keep (below the pre-registered 4 ms bar — the fp32 dy AG only costs ~3.7 ms at head — but zero-risk and the best-performing arm). `spf/001-backward-quick-wins` @ `2fc968f52` |
| SPF-002 owner-sharded psum_scatter dx return | Not a drop-in: `custom_vjp` pins dx to x's (replicated) sharding; with reshard-back it is +0.73 ms | **Falsified.** A real win needs x owner-sharded at the MLP boundary (training-integration change; folds into the source-push-dy / carveout design) |
| SPF-003a tip `26711f86e` grouped W13 gathers | 23.025 -> **22.769 ms** (75.45 useful), target checksum unchanged | Real but modest (-1.11%); gather still ~2.7x off the 8.4 ms inbox floor |
| SPF-003b fused W13-bwd zero-fill double-write fix | Bit-exact, but +0.32 ms vs control | **Falsified** — duplicate NVLink zero-writes were fully overlapped; reverted |
| SPF-004 combine via plain XLA gather-sum | **0.481 ms / 1745 GB/s**, bitwise-identical to the Pallas kernel, deterministic | **Adopt** (`spf/004-combine-roofline` @ `2ece2c284`); also W2 from_h weight-copy hoist kept (-3.9% stage) |
| SPF-005 host planner cost at target shape | `build_source_push_plan` **380 ms**; full public path **~1.85 s host work per plan**, rebuilt per routing per layer per microbatch | Confirmed ~190x over threshold: host planning dominates device time 6-30x on the public API; device-siding the planner (semantic JAX planner runs in-jit ~1.3-1.5 ms on GPU) is the top structural priority |

New issues found while measuring:
- **SPF-006**: reduced-shape fused-W13 compare `valid_error_count` regressed 0 -> 5 -> 3 somewhere in `d2ce47ca35..088831b4b` (72 commits); blocks promotion from that segment until bisected.
- **SPF-007**: staged w2_return stage regressed **4.05 -> 7.08 ms** at branch head vs the 2026-07-03 measurement — larger than all S-tier wins combined; needs a bisect.
- Full-forward `--check` at target shape reports max_abs_diff=512.0 (pre-existing; all historical target gates ran `--no-check`).
- Iris: `/tmp/iris` port-lock dir owned by another OS user breaks auto-tunnel for everyone else (`iris/cluster/backends/types.py:70-97` swallows PermissionError per port); and the current `cuda_toolchain_setup_script` `--offline` cudnn reinstall fails on cold-cache nodes.

State of the ladder: honest API 63.0 -> 61.0 ms (SPF-001); combine and W2-hoist wins live on the forward path; `ring` (38.2 ms / 202 useful) still leads. Next highest-leverage: bisect SPF-007, then avenue 7 (source-push dy; requires the owner-sharded-x boundary change SPF-002 exposed) and the avenue-10 SM-carveout design.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 **SPF-007 resolved — no bisect needed.** The w2_return 4.05 → 7.08 ms "regression" is a single step change with a contemporaneous paper trail, not branch drift:

- 4.050 ms logged at `89f3267fc` (2026-07-03 13:12) with the post-SwiGLU `_sharded_w2_return_direct_to_source_kernel`.
- `ae1c9aed1` "Wire source-push forward through H" + `e8fbfa85e` "Fix source-push W2-from-H lowering" (17:39/17:59 the same day) switched the staged forward to `_sharded_w2_from_h_return_direct_to_source_kernel` so the MLP-level custom VJP gets its H-checkpoint residual.
- 7.048 ms was measured at 18:04 that evening and attributed to the W2-from-H prologue (`6597-moe-mgpu-forward.md:4623`); head measures 7.077 ms — the other ~250 commits in the range contributed ~nothing.

Mechanism (from the kernel diff): ~2.5× M-side GMEM traffic (gate+up = 2I vs I, plus a k-invariant route-weight tile reloaded every k iteration until the SPF-004 hoist), a serial fp32 SwiGLU through an extra SMEM round-trip between TMA and WGMMA, and a single-buffered k-loop with `wgmma_wait(0)` inside — no overlap of loads/elementwise/wgmma.

Reclassified from "regression bisect" to **avenue 8 kernel work**, with a sharpened plan: (1) move route scaling to the output tile — exact algebra, `(diag(w)·A)·W2 = diag(w)·(A·W2)` — deleting `weight_smem` from the loop; (2) double-buffer + deferred `wgmma_wait` so SwiGLU overlaps the next tile's TMA. Direct-kernel parity is not expected (2× hidden bytes is inherent to the H boundary), but roofline says only ~1 ms of the +3 ms is bytes; ~4.5–5 ms vs 6.80 ms post-hoist looks reachable.

Logbook: SPF-007 entry on `research/mcwitt/6841-source-push-followup` (`2926b0f78`).

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 **SPF-008 — avenue-8 executed: output-side route scaling adopted (w2_return 7.08 → 6.36 ms); double-buffering falsified by occupancy**

Branch `spf/008-w2-from-h-kernel` (off PR head `26711f86e`, tip `882f2d3d5`).

**Adopted (`aa38972c8`).** The route weight is per-row, so `(diag(w)·A)·W2 = diag(w)·(A·W2)`: the from_h/from_compact_h kernels now scale the fp32 accumulator once after the k-loop instead of multiplying the weight into every activation tile. This deletes the k-invariant weight-tile reload (subsumes the SPF-004 hoist), the host-side `[rows, block_k]` route-weight expansion, and one multiply per element in the serial SwiGLU. The 2026-07-03 "cannot load the block_m=64 route-weight vector" lowering blocker does not apply post-GEMM — `mgpu.load(..., Layout.WGMMA.reduce(1))` + broadcast into the accumulator lowers fine.

Measured (`/marin/spf008-mid-aa38972c8`, 216 profile, staged_host_sync, roughly_balanced cf1.25, 5 repeats): **w2_return 6.355 ms** (head 7.077, hoist 6.803), **total 15.970 ms** (head 16.724), w13 8.576, combine 0.898. Numerics: reduced-shape `--check` max_abs_diff `0.00048828125`, bit-identical to the pre-change 2026-07-03 smoke. H100 `-k source_push` pytest: same `2 failed, 13 passed` as unmodified head (both failures pre-existing, confirmed by control job `/marin/spf008-headctl-pytest-26711f86e`).

**Falsified (`2c0f60a70`, reverted).** The planned 2-stage double-buffered k-loop with deferred `wgmma_wait(1)` made it **worse**: 8.573 ms (`/marin/spf008-tipbench-2c0f60a70`). Doubling pipeline SMEM 80→160 KB/CTA halves co-resident CTAs per SM from 2 to 1, and the inter-CTA interleaving that was hiding the serial TMA→SwiGLU→wgmma chain is worth more than the intra-CTA pipeline. Lesson: overlap schemes for these Lane kernels must stay under ~112 KB/CTA (2 CTAs/SM) — in-place activation staging or warp specialization, not naive full double-buffering.

**Where this leaves avenue 8**: from_h floor is ~5.0 ms (direct 4.05 + ~1 ms inherent H-boundary bytes); 6.36 achieved; ~1.4 ms of serialization overhead remains for an occupancy-neutral design. Logbook entry: SPF-008 on `research/mcwitt/6841-source-push-followup`.

issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
## Goal

Use a supported PyTorch CUDA 13 build alongside JAX CUDA 13, and keep only the direct version pins that protect a demonstrated compatibility boundary. The uv lock should provide reproducibility; package requirements should use ranges where safe.

## Current blocker

`marin-core[gpu]` currently resolves:

- JAX on CUDA 13 with `nvidia-cublas>=13.2.0.9`.
- PyTorch 2.11 from the cu128 index with separate CUDA 12 runtime packages.

The PyTorch cu130 wheel cannot replace cu128 as-is: it requires `cuda-toolkit[cublas]==13.0.2`, which pins `nvidia-cublas==13.1.0.3` and conflicts with Marin’s B200 cuBLAS floor.

## Work

1. Find a supported PyTorch CUDA 13 resolution that retains Marin’s H100 NCCL and B200 cuBLAS guards. Prefer a newer compatible release over overriding an upstream exact CUDA-library dependency.
2. Audit the direct GPU requirements for `torch`, `torchvision`, and the CUDA libraries:
   - Document why each exact pin or bounded range is necessary.
   - Replace exact application-level pins with compatible ranges where the lockfile and upstream dependency metadata are sufficient.
   - Keep hardware safety floors such as cuBLAS/NCCL until validation proves they are obsolete.
3. Update the PyTorch index selection and uv lock.
4. Validate imports, device execution, matmul, and collectives on H100 and B200; run the existing H100 GPU canary.

## Acceptance criteria

- `marin-core[gpu]` installs one coherent CUDA 13 environment without per-job overrides.
- PyTorch and TorchVision resolve as a compatible pair.
- The resolved cuBLAS and NCCL versions retain the existing B200 and H100 fixes.
- Every remaining direct exact pin has a nearby compatibility rationale; otherwise it is expressed as the narrowest validated range.
- H100 and B200 smoke tests pass, and the H100 GPU canary passes.

<details>
<summary>Why the current constraints exist</summary>

- **Torch 2.11:** selected in #5379 because Torch 2.10 cu128 pinned NCCL 2.27.5, which reproduced a CoreWeave H100 all-to-all failure. Torch 2.11 cu128 brought NCCL 2.28.9, which passed the probe.
- **TorchVision 0.26:** this is the native-extension compatibility pair for Torch 2.11. PR #6346 demonstrated why changing Torch without changing TorchVision is unsafe.
- **cuBLAS floor:** `nvidia-cublas>=13.2.0.9` was added in #5428 after older CUDA 13 builds warned on B200. Marin does not directly exact-pin cuBLAS; uv records the selected version in the lock.
- **cu128 index:** retained because the available Torch cu130 metadata exact-pinned cuBLAS below that B200 floor.
- **vLLM:** the selected vLLM revision also pins its build/runtime Torch and TorchVision pair exactly. Relaxing Marin alone may therefore not be enough for GPU vLLM; any required fork change belongs with #7135.

</details>

Blocks #7135. The downstream `marin-serve --gpu` integration remains tracked by #7111.

comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖 Cross-ref from PR #7303 (merged).

#7303 completed `serve_and_eval`'s GPU vLLM path by overlaying Marin's forked CUDA vLLM onto the serve venv (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 … --torch-backend=cu130 "vllm @ git+<fork>@<rev>" runai-model-streamer[s3]`), then serving it with the default `WorkspaceVllm` launcher. Its note reads "drop the overlay for `marin-core[vllm-gpu]` once #7134 lands."

On #7303, @rjpower asked us to reconsider that target. Rather than wait on a managed `vllm-gpu` extra, the direction is to productionize the launcher path: extend the isolated CUDA vLLM launcher already merged in #7133 with a source selector (`VllmType {UPSTREAM, MARIN_FORK}`), so `marin.inference` serves both stock and fork vLLM through one `uvx` launcher — chosen by the model, not the accelerator. (Design + diagrams in the artifact; discussion mirrored on #7135.)

Directly relevant to this issue: the overlay runs `--torch-backend=cu130`, which is exactly what a managed `gpu` extra cannot carry today. The extra is pinned to the `pytorch-cu128` index because cu130's cuBLAS sits below Marin's B200 floor (`nvidia-cublas>=13.2.0.9`) — this issue's own stated blocker. An isolated `uvx` launcher runs cu130 in a throwaway env without dragging cuBLAS into the workspace resolution, so it can retire the #7303 overlay *without* first resolving the CUDA-13 unification.

Net: #7134 stays valuable for a single coherent managed GPU image, but it is no longer the blocker for the serve/eval path — that path can standardize on the launcher independently.

Full research, project-dependency diagrams, and the proposed design: https://loom.oa.dev/s/ms4p9i4w/artifacts/vllm-serve-productionization

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment explored whether free generation from strong base models can reveal pretraining coverage gaps that ordinary evals miss. The infrastructure direction made progress: a TPU-native sampler and latent-topic discovery path were prototyped, and smoke runs wrote reusable artifacts. The main scientific result so far is negative for tokenizer-vocab bigrams: both `r1` and `r2` completed, but Qwen collapsed bare two-word prompts into generic explanatory continuations, with 43/48 prompts sharing the same first token in at least 75% of samples and no useful improvement from expanding from the original prompt. Do not keep tuning the content-word bigram path; if this line continues, use a weaker launch family or a scorer that discounts generic preambles and validates candidates with the pairwise BPB gap workflow.

### Helpful links
- Initial sampler implementation note: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4307017787
- First latent-topic smoke: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4316637640
- Bigram `r1` result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4316819223
- Bigram dead-end decision: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4317162165
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description
Use free generation from strong base models as an eval-discovery tool for pretraining blind spots. Start with Qwen3, then compare against Llama, Gemma, and other strong bases where available. The goal is to find surface-form families that strong models naturally continue but Marin may not cover well in Paloma, uncheatable evals, raw technical text, or capability eval slices.

This is hypothesis generation, not evidence by itself. Any sampled category should be checked against real held-out documents and then validated with pairwise gap/PPL before changing data mixtures.

## Hypothesis or Goal
Sampling with both empty prompts and seeded prefixes will surface missing or under-covered distributions such as raw URLs, package metadata, tables, logs, schemas, notebooks, compiler output, non-English technical docs, citations, mixed prose-code formats, and unusual whitespace/layout patterns. Agent-assisted clustering can turn samples into candidate eval slices, but each cluster needs a real source and a coverage decision: already covered, add eval only, add data work, or ignore.

### Links
* Parent confidence epic: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5005
* Gap finder: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4934
* Raw technical text: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4961
* Capability evals: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4963

## Results

comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Fetch issue and linked context (#5005, #4934, #4961, #4963)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight against open PRs/issues
- [x] Survey existing generation, eval, and gap-report infra on main

- [ ] Awaiting human sign-off before implementation (scope > 100 LOC; do not open a parallel PR)

**Research**

Out of scope for a single small PR — this is a multi-stage research workflow (free generation → clustering → surface-form labels → validation via pairwise BPB). Gating dependency: the byte-aligned perplexity-gap report referenced in the linked runs has not landed on `main` yet; it lives on `codex/perplexity-gap-finder` at `890b8b2e7` and is tracked by #4934. Sampling work can start now, but validation hooks need #4934 to merge first (or to land as part of this effort).

Duplicate-work check: no overlapping open PR or issue. #4961 is the downstream data-work consumer; #4963 is the downstream eval-register consumer. This issue owns only the hypothesis-generation pipeline that feeds both.

**Relevant code**
- [`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py) — native/Docker vLLM sidecar, TPU+GPU
- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx) — async_vllm / vllm / levanter sampling backends
- [`lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/uncheatable_eval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/uncheatable_eval.py) — raw held-out docs template (Wikipedia, GH, arXiv, BBC)
- [`experiments/evals/exp1600_uncheatable_evals.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/exp1600_uncheatable_evals.py) — raw-doc PPL eval flow (wiring template)
- `codex/perplexity-gap-finder@890b8b2e7` — byte-aligned BPB gap report (blocked on #4934 landing)

Gaps on `main`: no free-generation harness, no embedding/clustering pipeline, no surface-form categorizer, and no gap report to validate against until #4934 lands.

**Proposed Approach**

Land this as three independently reviewable PRs rather than one blob.

PR 1 — `strong_model_sampler` (~300 LOC). New module at `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/coverage_sampler.py`. Thin wrapper over the existing vLLM backend in `inference_ctx/vllm.py` that drives a configured strong base (Qwen3-8B first, then Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B) over two prompt regimes: (a) empty / BOS-only, (b) short seeded prefixes drawn from Paloma + Uncheatable domain samples. Output: sharded JSONL of `{model, prompt_regime, seed_source, sample_text, logprobs_summary}` on GCS. Config is a dataclass (no env-var dispatch); reuses `VllmServerHandle` — do not fork a parallel inference path.

PR 2 — `sample_clustering` (~400 LOC). New module at `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/coverage_clustering.py`. Embed samples with a small off-the-shelf encoder (bge-small or e5-small via HF), cluster with HDBSCAN, then have an agent label each cluster with a surface-form tag (URLs, package metadata, tables, logs, schemas, notebooks, compiler output, non-English technical docs, citations, mixed prose-code, unusual whitespace). Output: parquet of `{cluster_id, label, examples, size, source_models}` plus an HTML report. No new provider SDK — reuse `anthropic` or the existing eval-LLM plumbing for labeling.

PR 3 — `coverage_gap_validation` (~200 LOC, gated on #4934). For each labeled cluster, pull matched real documents from Paloma + Uncheatable + `datakit/download/*` and run the byte-aligned BPB gap report from #4934. Emit a per-cluster verdict: `already_covered` / `add_eval_only` / `add_data_work` / `ignore`. Wire into `experiments/evals/` as `exp_coverage_gap_discovery.py` mirroring `exp_model_perplexity_gap_marin_vs_llama.py`.

Scope caveats worth sign-off before coding:

1. Strong-model list: start with Qwen3-8B-Base only; Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B-base as a fast-follow once the pipeline works end-to-end. Confirm licensing for redistribution of sampled text (Gemma terms in particular).
2. Cluster labeling: agent-assisted labels are hypotheses, not ground truth — surfaced in the report as such, and the coverage verdict must come from #4934 BPB gap, not from cluster size.
3. Do not commit sampled text to the repo; write to `gs://marin-us-central2/experiments/coverage_sampling/` and register via `ExecutorStep`.
4. Preflight: 10–50k samples per model, truncated at 2k tokens. Cost estimate ~1 TPU-hour per model on v5p-8 for generation, plus CPU-only clustering.

Open question for maintainer before I start: should the strong-model sampler reuse `rl.rollout_worker` (heavier, battery-included) or a new thin client on `inference_ctx.vllm` (lighter, no RL coupling)? Leaning toward the latter to avoid pulling RL deps into the eval path.

Result:

- Experiment page: https://marin.community/data-browser/experiment?path=gs%3A//marin-us-central1/experiments/exp_coverage_gap_discovery-5de081.json

- Completed successfully on April 24, 2026 at 3:40 PM PDT.

Comparison vs `r1`:
- `r1` (`discovered_topic` expansion): `48/64` unique completions overall.
- `r2` (`discovery_prompt` expansion): `45/64` unique completions overall.
- The selected topic shortlist is effectively the same between the two runs; representative topics are still things like:
  - `state of matter is determined by the balance between the kinetic energy`
  - `The term expenses identifier typically refers to a unique`
  - `A nickname marketplace is a platform where individuals can buy`
- `r2` keeps the original bigram prompt as the expansion seed (for example `Physical aggregate`, `expenses identifier`, `nickname marketplace`), but the resulting completions still snap to the same generic explanatory continuations.

Current read:
- Tokenizer-derived bigrams are a real topic-agnostic prompt family, but they are not yet producing the unknown-unknown behavior we want.
- The failure mode is now stable across both expansion modes: Qwen maps many plausible two-word seeds into high-prior explanatory/documentary templates rather than revealing recurring latent domains across prompts.

Next likely move:
- Stop selecting by per-prompt support and instead rank by recurrence across different prompt families.
- Or add a much weaker lexical launch family (e.g. unigram / punctuation / structural fragments) plus a cross-prompt novelty filter, because the current bigrams appear too semantically committed.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Additional read on the vocab-bigram runs: the opening-token collapse is real in the raw discovery samples, not just an artifact of topic extraction.

From `r2` (`gs://marin-us-central1/evaluation/coverage_sampling/Qwen--Qwen3-8B-Base-coverage-gap-discovery-latent_topic-6c786d45-971b43/`):
- 43 / 48 discovery prompts had the same first whitespace token in at least 75% of their 16 discovery samples.
- 41 / 48 had the same first two whitespace tokens in at least 75% of samples.
- 32 / 48 were still collapsed through the first three tokens at that threshold.

Concrete examples:
- `Physical aggregate` -> all 16 discovery samples start with `state of matter ...`
- `expenses identifier` -> all 16 start with `The term "expenses identifier" ...`
- `Parliament attacks` -> all 16 start with `the government for its handling ...`

This makes the current read sharper:
- the bigram path is not failing because of summary truncation alone;
- Qwen is assigning extremely peaked next-token distributions to these bare noun-phrase prompts;
- that means we probably need a weaker launch family or a scorer that ignores the generic explanatory preamble and compares later divergence instead.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Decision: the tokenizer-vocab bigram line is a dead end for #5006's actual goal.

Why:
- `r1` and `r2` both completed successfully, so this is not an infra or TPU-plumbing problem.
- Switching expansion mode did not help: `r1` had `48/64` unique completions overall, `r2` had `45/64`.
- The discovered topic shortlist was effectively unchanged between the two runs.
- The raw discovery samples themselves are heavily collapsed at the beginning:
  - `43/48` bigram prompts had the same first token in at least `75%` of discovery samples
  - `41/48` had the same first two tokens at that threshold
  - `32/48` were still collapsed through the first three tokens
- Representative failures are stable across both runs:
  - `Physical aggregate` -> `state of matter ...`
  - `expenses identifier` -> `The term "expenses identifier" ...`
  - `Parliament attacks` -> `the government for its handling ...`

Current read:
- Content-word bigrams are already too semantically committed for the unknown-unknown objective.
- Qwen maps them into very peaked explanatory/article continuations, so they do not reveal cross-prompt latent domains in the way we want.
- This should be recorded as a negative result and not tuned indefinitely.

If the search continues, the next branch should be something weaker than content-word bigrams or a scorer that explicitly discounts the generic explanatory preamble. But the tokenizer-vocab bigram path itself is not worth more time.

comments.body:
Mentioned by @ClassicLarry at https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5151#issuecomment-4336418404 as a direction to explore, and again [on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1516857141514997881) in relation to the GLM-5.2 release.

There was also a brief discussion of MLA in 2025 [on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1380235124011958313/1397673126854267012), summarized by Claude:
  - What MLA buys you: willheld — "for MLA, the inference benefit is mostly in RAM… because you 
  don't need to save the KV cache, just the latent cache." The win is serving memory, not loss.
  - The RoPE incompatibility (the central design wrinkle for your issue): "RoPE would mean you 
  need to materialize the full K vectors and therefore make MLA bad. So DeepSeek and Kimi folks 
  do just a tiny bit of RoPE to add some positional signal with a smaller perf cost." (msg
  (https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1380235124011958313/1397673126854267012)) —
  i.e. the decoupled/partial-RoPE trick. He pointed at Jianlin Su's kexue.fm
  (https://kexue.fm/archives/10862) (the RoPE author, now at Kimi), and a follow-up post
  (https://kexue.fm/archives/11111) arguing partial RoPE should be theoretically better.
  - The evaluation problem (flagged by dlwh, still unresolved): "we need to figure out how to 
  evaluate these inference-time things. KV reuse, MLA, GQA, alternating SWA… we want to know the
  bpb hit, and inference time/space can be its own measurement." willheld concurred the
  partial-RoPE effect is "not too likely to show up in C4 loss" — so a fair MLA eval needs
  long-context signal plus a separate inference time/space measurement, not just BPB.
  - willheld said he "planned to run MLA" after his then-current work — but no run ever surfaces
  in the corpus, so this didn't land.

comments.body:
I think we still want to explore MLA so going to reopen this issue. Also I had Mumwelt read through the [MLAfication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17202) paper and compare it to our work on MLA: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/hammer/4bf21985183ebae3cbee1e3e0c9f2d70/raw.

> Ideas worth trying
> 1. Calibrated KNorm in Larry's MLA stack. This is the cheapest test, and it answers the QK-norm problem that both Larry and Will raised.
> 
> Experiment: train the fast-track MLA + Inkling model with per-head key norm, swap in the calibrated constants at the end, and measure the loss change. Compare against the current stack without QK-norm.
> Also compare against [QK-Normed MLA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16310), which [Larry cited](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1527756652890161292/1551997294805520455) as another way to keep QK-norm under MLA. In the same thread Kaiyue Wen relayed Jianlin Su's concern that keeping QK-norm under MLA grows the KV cache. A fixed constant should not.
>
> 2. Pretrain with MHA, convert to MLA for serving. This is the route that would win back Larry's 15%.
> 
> Experiment: pretrain a fast-track MHA model (with QK-norm and half-RoPE) at d1024–d1280. Convert it to a latent the size of the GQA 4:1 cache (a 75% cut), and distil on about 1–2% of the training tokens.
> Success test: the converted model beats GQA 4:1 trained from scratch, at equal KV memory.
> The joint SVD initialisation may also be what the staircase lacked, since that run's latent steps started from random weights.
> It needs a Levanter port. The math is small: the norm constants, the weighted SVD, and attention-only distillation. Marin already runs distillation, including on-policy distillation ([#9920](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920)).
> Precedent is mixed. The one previous surgery on a trained Grug MoE, tying expert banks across layers, [recovered most of the loss but missed its targets](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8032).

🤖 No. The current Grug production hero (`hero-ctx16k-step257k`) uses GQA softmax attention, with 48 query heads, 12 local KV heads, and 6 global KV heads. Its [attention module](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L538-L578) has separate Q, K, and V projections; the [hero recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py#L85-L115) selects the FA4 kernel. The recipe's `latent_dim=3072` is [LatentMoE](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1102-L1115): it compresses expert-parallel transport, not the attention KV cache.

The [MFU handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9960) moved the hero to an optimized MoE stack; the earlier [FA4 handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9378) changed its attention kernel. issues.author: hammer
issues.body:
TL;DR

Marin has not trained or evaluated any model on computer use: operating desktop, mobile or browser applications. Two Alibaba papers from this week release pieces a text-only model could use. This issue proposes RL on MAI-Gym's 42 synthetic apps through their text observation mode, and a computer-use baseline on OSWorld-v2 with OpenGCUA's code-first harness. Pixel-based tasks wait for vision support. No experiments have run yet.

Marin's agent post-training covers function calling, terminal and SWE tasks. Nothing covers graphical applications:

- No computer-use benchmark (OSWorld, AndroidWorld, WebArena) appears in the current eval policy ([#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197)). The nearest evals are the terminal benchmarks Terminal-Bench 2.1 and OT-TBLite.
- The harnesses we train and evaluate with (Terminus-2, Pi, mini-swe-agent, OpenCode) expose shell, file and function-call tools only. On these tasks, the Antidoom step-12 checkpoint of Snowball, Marin's post-trained 67B-A2B MoE, scores 31.1% on SWE-bench Verified and 10.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 ([#10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040#issuecomment-6158094013)).
- [#7418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7418) listed the web and OS agent sources from OpenThoughts-Agent (Mind2Web, go-browse, Synatra, nnetnav-live, AgentTuning WebShop/ALFWorld/OS). It left them unconverted because they need an interactive runtime to verify. All are text-only. The issue closed on October 6 in favour of sourcing our own RL data.
- Our models cannot read screenshots. Rui Li's SigLIP2 + Qwen3 baseline ([#2383](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2383)) did not merge. bkolligs is connecting SigLIP to Delphi 998M ([#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524), [PR #10076](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10076), open) and has no benchmark numbers yet.
- Shellbox machines return text and bytes only ([`machine.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L211-L248)). The QEMU backend is a headless microVM, and nobody has measured whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our nodes ([#9433](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9433)).
- Our largest sandbox run reached about 2,150 live gVisor sandboxes before the controller of Iris, our cluster scheduler, saturated ([#10111](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10111)). Work to move execution off the controller is open ([#10119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10119)).

TaskForge ([#10152](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10152)), our RL task generator, validates each task by replaying reference solutions and running agents that look for shortcuts. Its tasks so far are math and science problems in shells.

MAI-Gym

[MAI-Gym](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939) (Tong et al., 2026) runs GUI agents for evaluation and online RL through one rollout pipeline:

- Environments: Android in ReDroid containers, which avoids the nested virtualization the standard emulator needs; desktop VMs inside containers; headless Chromium for web. It reaches 20,000 parallel instances with warm pools and screenshots passed through object storage.
- Actions: coordinate clicks, typing and hotkeys, plus `bash` on desktops. Observations are screenshots, plus shell output on desktops.
- Synthetic apps: coding agents build resettable mock apps and cross-app scenarios. A verifier must score 0 on the initial state, 1 after a reference solution and 0 after reset.
- Training: Qwen3.5-9B (a vision-language model), SFT then GRPO. MAI-Gym-9B scores 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified (desktop) and 78.4% on MobileWorld (Android).
- Transfer: RL in a mock of the 12306 train-ticketing app raised success on 52 tasks in the real app, on a physical phone, from 28.8% to 48.1%.

Only part of it is released. The repository has the agent harness and 42 synthetic apps with 840 tasks. The framework, the synthesis skills and the 2,000 OSWorld/MobileWorld tasks are announced but not yet published.

Each released app is one HTML file with a deterministic state machine. Its manifest declares a text observation (`engine.a11y(state)`) and actions by element ID (`tap {id}`, `type {id, text}`). Verifiers are JSON checks on the app's final state. A text-only model can therefore run these tasks in a headless browser, with no screenshots.

OpenGCUA

[OpenGCUA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) (Zhou et al., 2026) studies harness design for computer use with existing frontier models. It releases no trained model.

- At each step the model writes one Python program. The program may call `pyautogui`, `bash()` and `subprocess`, and the prompt prefers `bash()` to GUI actions.
- The paper moves two decisions from fixed harness rules to the model: when to take a screenshot, and how to track task state, which the model does with a todo list.
- On the 82 OSWorld-v2 tasks that need no internet access, the mean partial score of eight models rose from 45.3 with GUI-only batched actions to 64.9 with this code-first harness. Steps per task fell 53%. The weakest GUI-only models gained the most: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rose from 28.0 to 57.7.

The paper runs no text-only configuration, so we analysed its released trajectories. Models requested a screenshot in 26–60% of steps. Each model used no GUI actions on 4 to 18 tasks, and only 5 of the 82 tasks were solved by some model with neither GUI actions nor screenshots. A text-only model would solve few of these tasks, but the shell-first design matches what our models already do well.

Licences

- MAI-Gym's repository has no licence file, so the apps and tasks need the authors' permission before we train on them.
- OpenGCUA's code is Apache-2.0. Its trajectories carry no licence, and most are outputs of closed models.
- OSWorld-v2 is Apache-2.0.

Goal: give Marin a computer-use evaluation and a first training signal for graphical applications, starting with interfaces a text-only model can use.

Hypotheses:

1. RL on a training split of MAI-Gym's synthetic apps, using text observations, raises Snowball's success on held-out apps. Function calling (BFCL-Parity), Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified do not regress.
2. With OpenGCUA's code-first harness and no screenshots, Snowball solves some of the 82 offline OSWorld-v2 tasks. That score is the text-only baseline a vision-capable model must beat.

Proposed steps:

1. Ask the MAI-Gym authors about licensing the apps and tasks.
2. Run the 42 apps in a headless browser behind a Shellbox backend that exposes the text observation and ID actions, with the existing verifiers as rewards. Hold out whole apps for evaluation, and check the tasks with TaskForge's validation. The same backend could later host the web sources from #7418.
3. Measure the Snowball baseline on the held-out apps, then run RL with Marin's rollout engine ([#9623](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9623)).
4. Check whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our Iris nodes. If it is, run OSWorld-v2 with the OpenGCUA harness in a desktop VM. Without KVM, the QEMU backend falls back to software emulation (TCG), which is slower.
5. Revisit pixel-based tasks when [#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524) produces a vision model at a useful scale.

Proposed. No owner yet. Computer use is not on any current roadmap.

Links

* Papers: [MAI-Gym, arXiv 2610.20939](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939); [OpenGCUA, arXiv 2610.22200](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200)
* MAI-Gym code and apps: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym) (apps in `site/apps/`); model: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B](https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B)
* OpenGCUA code: [Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA) (OSWorld agents in `packages/harness/examples/osworld/`); trajectories: [viewer](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/trajectories.html)
* Benchmark: [xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2](https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2)
* Android containers: [ReDroid](https://github.com/remote-android/redroid-doc)
* Related: [#10189](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10189) (web-search agents)

issues.author: WhenWen
issues.body:
Evaluate Copy-Paste Language Models on the original July MoE recipe. The copy head mixes the native vocabulary distribution with a causal distribution over observed tokens, sums repeated-token mass, and uses a learned sink to fall back to the vocabulary head. Packed documents remain isolated. Method: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19247v1.

The first d512, seed-0 validation at 1,000 updates improved the 23-domain macro NLL from 4.579368 to 4.092498 (-0.486869, 10.63%); all 23 domains improved. Native aggregate NLL was 4.387551 versus 3.858693. This is an early, single-seed observation, not a final quality or efficiency claim. The 10,980-update run is still running.

The paired protocol preserves the original July backbone, initialization, QB routing, MuonH/AdamH/Adam optimizer, sequence8192, batch16, tokenizer, training mixture and native validation. Recipe commit: 444b5ea66bda75b6dfc7746ff20c9dfec6ba159a; runtime: 3fd402a926c907d7cb87a04935e56db972652c48. The tiled target-only head adds 525,312 parameters at d512 and avoids materializing a batch × sequence × vocabulary copy distribution. Its attention arithmetic remains quadratic; speedup is not claimed.

Extend the comparison to d768, reusing completed control 2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0. This control has six layers, six query heads, one KV head, expert384/shared768 and deliberately retains the d512 optimizer heuristic. The candidate must keep that recipe, with 1,181,184 added copy-head parameters. Both widths use 10,980 updates (1,439,170,560 input tokens), seed0 and reserved v4-32. Report final and intermediate NLL, all domains, raw loss curves, wall time and throughput; do not equate token matching with compute matching.

Independent dense-mixture checks cover values, all six gradient paths, repeated/absent targets, future/document isolation and disabled-gate parity. All four d512 TPU workers passed BF16 fused-head checks before training. The synthetic precursor reduced loss but failed complete-output evaluation; it did not pass a task mastery gate.

Implementation/evidence: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/pull/152
Frozen protocol: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-moe-protocol.md
First curves and raw-evidence pointers: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-results.md
Live d512 run: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/auto-understanding-arch/runs/seed0-v1

The upstream contribution will keep the opt-in copy head and numerical tests separate from the default recipe. Generation/cache support and multiple-seed replication remain outside this initial NLL experiment. A merged implementation does not settle the research question.

Research provenance: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/151; originating task definition: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/99 (`ordered_paragraph_template@1`). Prior synthetic findings: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/149. These task records provide provenance; the July experiment evaluates native LM data.

# Proposed Fix

1. Recover the linked protocol and pin the exact recipe/runtime commits, dataset and tokenizer identities, validation domains, seeds, optimizer settings, and control/candidate checkpoint IDs for both widths; confirm the d768 control is `2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0` and preserve its d512 optimizer heuristic.

4. Publish intermediate and final paired NLL for all 23 domains and both aggregates, raw loss curves, exact token counts, wall time, throughput, parameter and copy-attention cost, and links to immutable configs/checkpoints; distinguish token-matched from compute-matched comparisons.
5. Decide from the final paired results whether the NLL gain justifies measured overhead, then submit a separate opt-in Marin implementation with numerical tests if warranted; leave generation/cache support and replication as explicit follow-ups.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://github.com/swesmith` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `codeload.github.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `https://140.82.112.3/`, `https://140.82.114.4/` (GitHub by IP) | 200 | TLS handshake cut | 200 |
| `https://1.1.1.1/` | 403 | TLS handshake cut | 403 |
| `pypi.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `www.google.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |

On these unchanged trees the verifier completed afterwards and scored 0, as expected. With GLM (`swe-net2`), 3/3 trials passed under the limit, and all 76 proxy calls returned 200. In one trial GLM ran `pip install pytest ...` and saw `No internet`.

**Tool-env leak:** in `swe-net2/swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity), GLM ran `sed -n '136,175p' /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`. A probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup on one task from each of the 36 repos (`toolenv2`). It found the same 80 distributions on every image. Only three of them are pool repos: pygments (222 tasks), pandas (196) and tenacity (30). Every conda-based image also ships conda's own `boltons-23.0.0` under `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs`, including the mahmoud/boltons image (21 tasks). The install is now pinned (`mini-swe-agent-2.1.0-constraints.txt`, sha256 `c67d1ee2…`, Python 3.12), so this set cannot drift between the pilot and the full run. SWE-smith ingestion also drops any trace whose commands or outputs touch `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/`.

**Run folders** (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/`):
- `netprobe2`, `netprobe3`, `netprobe4`: network probes; `agent/network_probe.json` per trial.
- `swe-net2`: GLM trials under the limit.
- `toolenv2`: tool-env listing; union in `tool_env.json`.

- **Pool:** every repo above is removed from pool v4. The SWE-smith family is topped back up to 2,100 from the 28 remaining repos, which the base-image check found clean. The method and per-repo evidence are in `image-check-v4.jsonl` and `manifest.json` `clean_copy_probe` (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/`, mirrored at [open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10@ac4e9c3f](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10/tree/ac4e9c3fee6612c1d8ceecb0aa22950c4bdd8a9a)).
- **Generation (#207):** mini-swe-agent installs with a pinned dependency set, so the tool env cannot drift. The agent phase runs without internet access (proxy host only), which also closes the public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors.
- **Training rows (#211):** the row builder drops any trace that touches mini-swe-agent's tool env, or that reads a library copy (site-packages, `_vendor`, conda pkgs, the Go module cache) of its task's own repo. Drops are counted per task.

Kimi and other existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ. A trace audit for these paths is still open.

- **Commands:** most hits are `git diff HEAD~1 -- <file>`, `git show <hash>`, `git show main:<file>`, `git diff main` and `git log -p`.
- **"Saw a fix line":** the terminal output after the history command contains a clean-code line from the task's bug patch (15+ characters, in a non-test file) that the agent had not typed earlier.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
When Harbor runs the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter on a SWE-smith task, the agent's own Python environment is installed inside the task sandbox at agent setup (`/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`). That environment contains clean, unbroken copies of three packages that are also SWE-smith task repositories: pygments, pandas and tenacity. The agent can read the fixed source directly. The same class exists at the image level, independent of the agent: conda's package cache ships boltons in every conda image, pip and setuptools vendor chardet, tomli and inflect, and one testbed environment holds an installed dataset egg.

Observed: in a GLM 5.3 trial on `swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity) with the mini-swe-agent adapter, the agent ran `sed -n 136,175p /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`, called it "the reference", copied the logic and passed. A pre-agent audit of the task packages cannot see this environment, because it appears only when the agent is installed.

Scope in the DCAgent SWE-smith packages (`DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`), measured with mini-swe-agent's dependencies pinned (identical 80 distributions across one image per repository): pygments 222 tasks, pandas 196, tenacity 30, boltons 21, chardet 10, tomli 23, inflect 27, dataset 13. In the 2,100-task shootout pool that was 542 tasks before replacement. A filename-only check produces false positives (pygments' `html.py` versus safety, IPython's `timing.py` versus alive-progress), so the check must compare module contents or names, not file suffixes.

Reproduce: start a trial with the mini-swe-agent adapter on any pygments, pandas or tenacity SWE-smith task, and in the agent phase list `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<package>/`. For the image-level copies, build the task's `environment/Dockerfile` and search outside `/testbed` for directories named after the task repository's import name (for example `find / -path /testbed -prune -o -type d -name tomli -print`).

Impact: pass rates on those tasks are inflated and the resulting traces teach reading a library copy instead of fixing the bug. Terminus-2 is not affected by the tool-environment copy, because the Terminus-2 agent runs outside the sandbox, but the image-level copies affect every agent. Existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ; they have not been audited for these paths.

Expected: during the agent phase, no readable copy of the task repository exists outside `/testbed`. Either the agent environment lives outside the sandbox (as Terminus-2 does), or the adapter installs it on a path the agent cannot read, or task packages whose repository is a dependency of the agent or of the base image are excluded from training pools and flagged in evaluation.

Done when: Harbor's mini-swe-agent adapter keeps its environment out of the agent's reach or documents the limitation; a content-based image check for repository copies outside `/testbed` is part of SWE-smith package validation; and existing SWE-smith trace sets are audited for reads under these paths. The shootout pool (#10213) already excludes the eight repositories above, pins the agent's dependencies, and drops traces that read a library copy of the task repository; the method and per-repository evidence are in the pool manifest at `open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10`. Related: #10212 (git history left in the same packages).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Harbor's Mini-SWE setup puts its Python tool environment inside the task container; a GLM 5.3 trial read the installed `tenacity/retry.py` and passed using that reference ([probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6227834962)). [Pool P v4](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6228022768) excludes the affected repositories, and its row builder drops known library-copy reads, but those controls apply to this shootout rather than to future SWE-smith packages or older traces. Marin delegates agent execution to the pinned Harbor runtime, so the adapter, package validator, and trace audit need separate changes.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L104-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L104-L116) — Harbor agent selection.
- [`driver_config.py#L69-L80`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L69-L80) — pinned external runtime.
- [`penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708) — one historical SWE-smith trace source.

# Proposal

Keep the v4 exclusions as the current safeguard. Add the following durable checks before treating other SWE-smith packages or historical traces as clean.

1. **Harbor adapter:** Move the Mini-SWE controller and its Python environment outside the task sandbox; send tool commands through Harbor's sandbox execution interface. Probe after agent setup, when the tool environment currently appears, and verify that the agent can edit `/testbed` but cannot read the controller's packages. If Harbor cannot support this boundary, document the limitation in the adapter and reject repository/agent pairs whose code ships in its pinned dependencies. The adapter change belongs in `marin-community/harbor`; Marin should pin the tested revision.
2. **Package validation:** Promote the [v4 image probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644) into the SWE-smith package build gate. Inspect agent-readable files outside `/testbed` in the built image and again after agent setup. Use repository import names and distribution metadata to find candidates, then confirm source overlap with content fingerprints; a matching filename alone must not reject a task. Record matched paths, files, image revision, and agent dependency pin in the manifest, and reject confirmed overlaps before publishing packages.
3. **Historical traces:** Inventory each existing SWE-smith trace source and its agent/setup revision, starting with the registered Penfever source and the Kimi traces noted in [#10212](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644). Join commands and observations to the task repository; flag reads from its copies in `site-packages`, `_vendor`, conda caches, eggs, Go module caches, and agent tool environments. Publish counts and example paths by dataset and repository, quarantine confirmed contaminated rows, and mark sources with missing command or environment provenance as unknown rather than clean. Run the audit where the traces are stored to avoid bulk cross-region transfer.

## Testing and rollout

Test the validator against the observed tenacity tool environment and vendored tomli, plus unrelated files such as Pygments' `html.py`; the latter must not trigger on its filename. Run one Mini-SWE task end to end with the new boundary and verify that setup, editing, and the verifier still work. Hand-check flagged and unflagged audit samples, publish the audit manifest and rejected counts, then require the validator result in future SWE-smith pool manifests.

## Costs and open question

Moving the controller changes Harbor's agent lifecycle and needs an integration test, while scanning built images adds package-build work. Can Harbor's current Mini-SWE adapter run outside the sandbox with its existing command transport? If not, the documented limitation plus enforced repository exclusions is the immediate adapter deliverable; the package gate and trace audit remain required.

## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

## Previous version notes

* Released Sept 24, 2026: 18 non-agentic benchmarks, 8 Harbor agentic benchmarks, and 4 reserved out-of-distribution benchmarks.
