MANAGED_SOURCE = Source(dataset="managed-agent", revision="0", row="0", importer_revision="0") """A ``TaskSpec`` requires provenance; an arbitrary attempt has none worth recording.""" class AttemptLimits(BaseModel): """The budget of one attempt: model replies, per-command and per-attempt wall clocks.""" model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid") max_turns: int = Field(gt=0, default=48) command_timeout: float = Field(gt=0, default=120.0) attempt_timeout: float = Field(gt=0, default=3600.0) startup_timeout: float = Field(gt=0, default=600.0) cleanup_timeout: float = Field(gt=0, default=60.0) class RolloutSpec(BaseModel): """What one agent attempt needs: a conversation to open, a machine to work in, and what to keep. ``grader`` is optional: without one the attempt is recorded ungraded. ``environment`` is optional: without one the agent has no machine and only the tools the harness gives it. """ model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid") id: str = Field(min_length=1) messages: tuple[Message, ...] environment: EnvironmentRequirements | None = None resources: ResourceGroups = Field(default_factory=ResourceGroups) output_paths: tuple[str, ...] = () grader: Grader | None = None limits: AttemptLimits = AttemptLimits() @dataclass(frozen=True) class AttemptOutcome: """One typed result per spec id: the rollout the engine produced, or why there is none.""" id: str rollout: RolloutData | None error: Exception | None = None @property def grade(self) -> GradeResult | None: return None if self.rollout is None else self.rollout.grade @dataclass(frozen=True) class Harness: """The tools an attempt's agent gets over its machine; ``shell_harness`` is the one most attempts want.""" name: str tools: Callable[[Machine | None, RolloutSpec], Sequence[AgentTool]] def shell_harness(*, output_limit_bytes: int = 16_384) -> Harness: """A harness whose only tool is the engine's shell, run on the attempt's machine.""" def tools(machine: Machine | None, spec: RolloutSpec) -> Sequence[AgentTool]: if machine is None: return () return (shell_tool(machine, timeout=spec.limits.command_timeout, output_limit_bytes=output_limit_bytes),) return Harness("shell", tools) def to_task(spec: RolloutSpec) -> TaskSpec: """The ``TaskSpec`` the engine runs for ``spec``: the one place the two contracts meet.""" events = tuple(TextMessage(role=m["role"], content=str(m.get("content", ""))) for m in spec.messages) return TaskSpec( id=spec.id, context=ConversationInput(events=events), environment_requirements=spec.environment or EnvironmentRequirements(), output_paths=spec.output_paths, answer_type=AnswerType.TEXT, answer_format=PlainText(), grader=spec.grader or NoGrader(reason="no grader declared for this managed attempt"), source=MANAGED_SOURCE, resources=spec.resources, ) def to_session(spec: RolloutSpec) -> TaskSessionSpec: limits = spec.limits return TaskSessionSpec( task_session=AGENT_SESSION, max_turns=limits.max_turns, model_turn_timeout=None, command_timeout=limits.command_timeout, tool_turn_timeout=None, total_turn_timeout=None, attempt_timeout=limits.attempt_timeout, verifier_timeout=limits.attempt_timeout, cleanup_timeout=limits.cleanup_timeout, ) class _EngineModel(ModelClient): """``ModelClient`` over the engine's completion: every turn the loop asks for is the engine's ``ModelTurn``. The engine samples through its own model function (the endpoint), keeps the served token ids, and hands the message back; the loop replays that message verbatim, so ``AgentTaskSession.advance`` sees the prefix it sent plus the turn and appends the tool observations instead of re-tokenising the conversation. """ def __init__(self, complete: AgentCompletion, tools: Sequence[AgentTool]): self._complete = complete self._options = {"tools": [tool.definition() for tool in tools]} if tools else {} async def complete(self, messages: Sequence[Message], policy: LLMPolicy) -> Completion: turn = await self._complete(SessionStart(messages=tuple(messages), options=self._options)) return _completion(turn) def _completion(turn: ModelTurn) -> Completion: message = turn.message calls = tuple( ToolCall(id=c["id"], name=c["function"]["name"], arguments=c["function"]["arguments"]) for c in message.get("tool_calls") or () ) finish = FinishReason.LENGTH if turn.stop_reason == "length" else FinishReason.TOOL_CALLS if calls else FinishReason.STOP return Completion( content=str(message.get("content") or ""), reasoning=str(message.get("reasoning_content") or ""), tool_calls=calls, finish_reason=finish, usage=NO_USAGE, wall_time=0.0, ) def agent_session(harness: Harness, spec: RolloutSpec, policy: LLMPolicy, record: CallLedger): """The ``TaskSessionFactory`` for ``spec``: the harness's loop inside the engine's session lifecycle.""" def factory(context: TaskSessionContext) -> AgentTaskSession: tools = harness.tools(context.machine, spec) async def loop(complete: AgentCompletion) -> None: await run_agent(_EngineModel(complete, tools), policy, spec.messages, tools, spec.limits.max_turns, record) return AgentTaskSession(loop, context.require_task_grader()) return factory class ManagedAgent: """Run a bounded set of independent attempts over one engine and yield one outcome per spec. Args: model: The engine's model function, the model endpoint bound outside. factories: Machine factories by backend, as ``RolloutEngine`` takes them. harness: The tools every attempt's agent gets. place: The machines ``spec`` runs on, chosen by the caller (laptop ShellSim, Iris gVisor). policy: The sampling policy the loop sends with every turn. record: Where model and tool calls are recorded. workers: Attempts in flight at once. """ def __init__( self, model: Callable[[ModelRequest], Awaitable[ModelTurn]], factories: Mapping[str, MachineFactory], harness: Harness, place: Callable[[RolloutSpec], TaskRuntimeSpec], policy: LLMPolicy, record: CallLedger, workers: int, ): self.model, self.factories, self.harness, self.place = model, factories, harness, place self.policy, self.record = policy, record self.gate = asyncio.Semaphore(workers) def lower(self, spec: RolloutSpec) -> tuple[LoweredTaskSpec, RolloutEngine]: sessions = {AGENT_SESSION: agent_session(self.harness, spec, self.policy, self.record)} engine = RolloutEngine(self.model, self.factories, sessions=sessions) return lower_task(to_task(spec), self.place(spec), to_session(spec), factories=self.factories, sessions=sessions), engine async def attempt(self, spec: RolloutSpec) -> AttemptOutcome: """One attempt, admitted through the gate; an engine error is the outcome, not an exception.""" async with self.gate: try: lowered, engine = self.lower(spec) return AttemptOutcome(spec.id, await engine.run(lowered)) except asyncio.CancelledError: raise except Exception as error: return AttemptOutcome(spec.id, None, error) async def run(self, specs: Iterable[RolloutSpec]) -> AsyncIterator[AttemptOutcome]: """Every spec's outcome, in completion order; cancelling the iterator cancels the attempts.""" done: asyncio.Queue[AttemptOutcome] = asyncio.Queue() pending = 0 async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group: for spec in specs: pending += 1 group.create_task(self._deliver(spec, done)) while pending: yield await done.get() pending -= 1 async def _deliver(self, spec: RolloutSpec, done: asyncio.Queue[AttemptOutcome]) -> None: done.put_nowait(await self.attempt(spec)) def shellsim_placement(backend: str = "shellsim") -> Callable[[RolloutSpec], TaskRuntimeSpec]: """The simplest placement: every machine on one backend, the verifier on the same when the grader needs one.""" def place(spec: RolloutSpec) -> TaskRuntimeSpec: machine = MachineRuntimeSpec( backend=backend, network="deny", cpus=None, memory_mb=None, storage_mb=None, gpus=0, user=None, startup_timeout=spec.limits.startup_timeout, cleanup_timeout=spec.limits.cleanup_timeout, ) verifier = machine if spec.grader is not None and getattr(spec.grader, "environment", None) else None return TaskRuntimeSpec(task_machine=machine if spec.environment else None, verifier_machine=verifier) return place ```

comments.body:
👨 I think I would use a slightly different interface for the "agent task" and maybe add `engine.run_agent`, but we can do that later.

<hr>

🤖 A proof of concept of `ManagedAgent` on the harness API of #10203 works with no change to the engine. A Zephyr job on cw-us-east-02a ran 10 GLM-5.3 agents that reviewed #10203, each with one focus, and a lead agent that checked their findings against the code. All 11 attempts ended with `stop` and no failure.

Code: [`experiments/post_training/managed_agent/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/rav/managed-agent-poc/experiments/post_training/managed_agent) on branch `rav/managed-agent-poc` (d74347f8d, on top of #10203 at d04b44ec8). Job: `/rav/managed-agent-poc-run-1`. Outputs: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/user/rav/projects/managed-agent-poc/run-1/` (`reviews.jsonl`, `lead_review.md`).

**Shape**

`ManagedAgent` is one `RolloutEngine`, one model, and a concurrency limit. It adds only admission: each attempt is `engine.run_task(spec, model)`, and `run(specs)` yields one `AgentOutcome(id, rollout, grade, failure)` for each spec, so that a failed attempt does not stop the others. `managed_agent.py` has 82 lines of code.

```python
harness = agent_harness(reviewer(pull_request, max_turns=limits.max_turns))  # the agent program
engine = RolloutEngine({}, {"reviewer": harness}, observer=ProgressLog())
manager = ManagedAgent(engine, ChatModel(glm_client, "glm-5.3", ...), concurrency=5)
specs = [agent_spec(agent_task(task_id, instructions), "reviewer", limits) for task_id, instructions in work]
async for outcome in manager.run(specs):
    ...  # outcome.answer, outcome.rollout, outcome.failure
```

- An attempt is a plain `TaskSpec`: the instructions in its public context, a text answer, and `NoGrader`. `agent_spec` gives it no machines and `TraceMode.MESSAGES`, because a chat endpoint renders its own tokens.
- The agent is an `agent_harness` program with its own tool loop and four read-only tools over the repository in the job bundle: `changed_files`, `file_diff`, `read_file`, and `search`. It sends the same options on each turn, so each request is a reply in one conversation.
- `ChatModel` (45 lines) serves each `ModelRequest` with an async OpenAI client, so the recorder can cancel a call at its deadline. It finds GLM through the Iris relay with `experiments/post_training/glm.py`.
- Zephyr shards the 10 specs to 2 workers, and each worker runs its shard with one `ManagedAgent` at concurrency 5. A second pipeline runs the lead agent. The workers get the GLM token from the job and find the relay themselves.

The engine already owns the hard parts: the limits, the record of each conversation, grading, cleanup, and events. Thus a managed agent needs no new `RolloutSpec` type, no new lowering, and no launcher. Zephyr and Iris place the workers.

**Run** (21:07 to 21:29 UTC: 10 minutes for the reviews and 10 minutes for the lead)

| agent | focus | turns | tool calls | prompt tokens | completion tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `review-00` | the recorder: its limits, its deadlines, and the end of an attempt | 18 | 20 | 361 k | 80 k |
| `review-01` | the agent harness: concurrent completion calls, cancellation, and agent shutdown | 20 | 23 | 543 k | 67 k |
| `review-02` | the public API: names, signatures, and what a harness author must know | 20 | 26 | 647 k | 48 k |
| `review-03` | the exact-token contract and the messages trace | 20 | 27 | 463 k | 48 k |
| `review-04` | failure handling: the operation that an interrupted attempt reports, and what its rollout keeps | 13 | 17 | 242 k | 39 k |
| `review-05` | grading: the task's grader, the host judge, and output capture | 20 | 34 | 580 k | 43 k |
| `review-06` | the tests: whether they test behavior, and which behavior has no test | 20 | 24 | 707 k | 4 k |
| `review-07` | the reference docs and docstrings: whether each sentence agrees with the code | 20 | 32 | 662 k | 59 k |
| `review-08` | simplicity: code, options, and types that the pull request can delete | 12 | 21 | 252 k | 7 k |
| `review-09` | downstream impact: what MarinSkyRL and other callers must change, and what can break without an error | 17 | 29 | 435 k | 30 k |
| `lead-review` | all | 16 | 25 | 435 k | 108 k |
| total | | 196 | 278 | 5.33 M | 533 k |

**What the agents found in #10203, after my check**

The lead confirmed 8 findings and rejected about 20, each with a reason. I checked the 8 against the code:

- 3 are false. `copy.deepcopy` and `model_copy` keep `judge_connection` (finding 6). `task_machine` does use `runtime.cleanup_timeout`, through `_prepare_machine` (finding 5). `TaskSpec` rejects a file or workspace answer with an in-process verifyit grader, so that grading failure cannot occur (finding 4).
- 1 is a documented limit: an agent that does not wait in `complete` can still run during grading. #10225 removes it.
- 4 are valid but small:
  - `record` after a refusal raises when no turn exists.
  - A pinned prompt that does not start with the served tokens is found only after the model answers, and the error blames the transport.
  - One sentence about the token budget is too strong.
  - No test has a host judge that hangs (#10246).

In the smoke run, the lead also reported a false finding about `SessionGrader`, which #10203 removes. Thus the lead review is a good triage of the 10 reviews, but each confirmed finding still needs a check.

**Gaps for a real version**

1. An `agent_harness` agent cannot read its `RolloutLimits`. Thus the reviewer gets `max_turns` two times: in the spec and in its closure. The agent harness can give the limits to the agent.
2. A reasoning model can use its whole token budget on its final turn and give no answer. In the smoke run, the one reviewer did this with `reasoning_effort=medium` and 32,768 tokens. The run uses the low effort for reviewers. An agent can also start a new conversation after a length stop, which the recorder permits.
3. `ChatModel` belongs in a library next to the engine, so that each managed agent does not write its own.
4. Arbitrary work fills the placeholders of `TaskSpec` (`Source`, `PlainText`, `NoGrader`). `agent_task` does this at one boundary, which is sufficient for now.

<details><summary>The lead review</summary>

# Review: [rolloutengine] Replace task sessions with registered harnesses

## Summary

The harness/recorder split is a real simplification: the recorder owns the model calls, limits, and token evidence outside the attempt deadline; the engine owns machines, grading, and cleanup; and the test suite asserts on recorded evidence rather than exit codes. Most of the deadline, refusal, and finalization logic I traced holds together exactly as documented. The confirmed problems cluster in four places: the agent harness can return while the agent task is still running (so the engine grades a workspace the agent may still be mutating), the documented "record a final reward after a refusal" pattern raises when the refusal was the attempt's first request, the pinned-token prefix contract is neither checked before sending nor checked at all in `MESSAGES` mode, and a check-time gap lets file/workspace-state answers with an in-process verifyit grader through to a guaranteed grade-time failure. Two doc/code contradictions (`task_machine`'s ignored `runtime.cleanup_timeout`, `judge_connection` dropped by `deepcopy`) and the budget wording round it out. No blockers.

## Confirmed findings

1. **Should fix — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/agent.py:55-66` (with `engine.py:187-189` and `docs/references/task-rollouts.md:220-222`).** When `completions.ended` wins the `asyncio.wait` race (a completion in another task — e.g. an HTTP handler — hit a model failure or limit), `run` returns while the agent task is still alive; the agent is only cancelled by the cleanup callback registered at `agent.py:58`, which runs *after* grading. Only calls inside `complete` are parked on `released`; an agent that is elsewhere can still run commands on `context.machine` while the engine captures `output_paths` and grades, contradicting the doc's safety claim, which covers only a *waiting* agent. Fix: when `ended` wins, cancel (or join, bounded by the cleanup deadline) the agent task before returning, so the record is final only when the agent is quiescent. (review-01 #1, review-02 #2)

2. **Should fix — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py:221-246` and `248-263` (docstring at `harness.py:84-98`).** The documented pattern "After `LimitReached` or a failed model request, the harness can still add data and metrics … to the step of the last turn until it returns" raises `RuntimeError` when the refusal was the attempt's *first* request (`_add_to_ended_step` finds no step anywhere), so a harness written to the docs (`except RolloutEnded: recorder.record(data=reward)`) converts a `MODEL` failure into a harness `PREPARE` failure — and since grading is gated on `failure[0] == RolloutOperation.MODEL` (`engine.py:187`), the completed turns are then not graded. Also, `record` checks `_ended()` first (line 228), so a deadline that expires in that window raises `RolloutEnded` instead of the promised amend. Fix: make `record(data=..., metrics=...)` a no-op (or attach to a synthetic terminal step) when the refusal left no step, and narrow the docstring to what the code does. (review-00 #3, review-04 #3)

3. **Should fix — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py:207-219` (docstrings at `harness.py:75-82`, `contracts.py:229-230`; check at `trace.py:73-74`).** `reply(..., token_ids=...)` documents that pinned tokens "must start with the tokens served so far" but never validates it. In `EXACT_TOKENS` mode the violation surfaces only after the model answers, as `RolloutContractError("Model transport changed the served token prefix")` — blaming the transport for a harness error — and is recorded as a model failure ("The model turn broke the token contract", `recorder.py:344-347`). In `MESSAGES` mode `_MessageTrace.append` performs no prefix check at all, so a wrong pin passes silently. Fix: check `token_ids[:len(trace.prefix)] == trace.prefix` in `reply` before sending and raise `RolloutContractError` directly, and either enforce or scope the doc sentence for `MESSAGES`. (review-03 #1 and #5, review-08 reply nit, review-09 #6)

4. **Should fix — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py:77-78` (with `checks.py:42-52` and `taskcompendium/grading.py:84-95`).** The in-process verifyit branch builds `GradingAttempt(conversation, stop_reason=...)` and drops `outputs`; `answer_submission` raises `TypeError` for any non-conversation, non-STATE answer. A task with `answer_type` FILE or WORKSPACE_STATE, a `VerifyitGrader` without an environment, and a selected task machine passes `check_spec` (only STATE and judge-with-non-conversation answers are rejected) and then interrupts *every* attempt with a `GRADE` failure. Fix: reject in-process verifyit graders on file/workspace-state answers in `check_spec`, as the judge branch already does, or pass `outputs` through. (review-05 #1)

5. **Should fix — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/machines.py:222-228` (and `docs/references/task-rollouts.md:428`).** The `task_machine` docstring (and the reference table) says "`runtime.cleanup_timeout`, when it is set, replaces `cleanup_timeout` for the machine's close," but the code builds `cleanup = _Cleanup(cleanup_timeout)` once and never reads `runtime.cleanup_timeout`; a caller relying on the sentence gets the argument deadline with no error. Fix: honor the override (e.g. `runtime.cleanup_timeout if runtime.cleanup_timeout is not None else cleanup_timeout`) or delete the sentence from both docs. (review-09 #1; the untested-claim half is review-06's task-machine nit)

6. **Should fix — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/spec.py:77-89` (with `grading.py:45-51`).** `__getstate__` also strips `judge_connection` from `copy.copy`/`copy.deepcopy`, not only from `model_dump`, JSON, and pickle as the field docstring and the reference doc claim. A worker pool that deep-copies specs silently loses the explicit connection and falls back to `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_BASE_URL`/`VERIFYIT_JUDGE_API_KEY` — potentially a *different* judge, with no error or diagnostic, which is exactly the round-tripping workflow the PR description calls out. Fix: keep the connection under copy/deepcopy (override `__deepcopy__`) or at minimum document that copy drops it, and consider recording when the connection came from the environment. (review-02 #4, review-09 #2)

7. **Nit — `docs/references/task-rollouts.md:445-448` (and `spec.py:47-49`, `recorder.py:348-352`).** The budget invariant "it never sends a request whose prompt alone reaches the budget" does not hold: the refusal test uses the just-completed request's prompt+response count as a stand-in for the next prompt, and the next prompt additionally contains the new observation tokens, so when the observations exceed the previous request's count, `spent_tokens + turn.request_tokens < max_total` can hold while the next prompt alone reaches the threshold. Fix: weaken the two doc sentences to say the check is a lower bound (or charge the projected next prompt), and clarify the recorder comment, which also does not say the current request is counted twice. (review-07; comment clarity from review-03 #3)

8. **Nit — `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py:70-76` and the judge tests in `lib/rolloutengine/tests/test_rollout.py` (~2922).** The judge tests exercise only a server that answers every request immediately with 200, so the documented bounds on the host-judge path — the verifier deadline stopping the engine's wait for a hanging judge, `JudgeSpec.request_timeout`, and the retry count — have no test. Fix: add a test with a handler that never responds (bounded by `verifier_timeout`, reported as a grading timeout) and one that fails so the retry count is observable in `judge_server.requests`. (review-06 #1 and #2)

## Rejected findings

- **review-00 #1 (total-turn timeout armed only at the first `start`):** the reference already documents that the total-turn deadline excludes the harness's work before its first request (`task-rollouts.md:430`), and the engine bounds that window with `attempt_timeout`; standalone `harness_rollout` documents that attempt deadlines belong to the engine.
- **review-00 #2 (tool deadline wins over the total deadline):** the two timeouts share one task and the first to fire cancels it, so both cannot be expired when the checks run; the ordering is unreachable in practice.
- **review-00 #4 (close leaves an expired model call's task awaiting forever):** speculative — it requires a transport that swallows the `model_turn_timeout` cancellation and never returns; the `call.expired()` guard itself is required because `reschedule` raises once expired.
- **review-01 #2 (cached turn returned after the record is final):** the cached return is guarded by `not self.ended.done()` with no await between the check and the return; any residual hazard of the agent running late is finding 1.
- **review-01 #3 (stop's release-then-cancel window):** `released.set()` and `agent.cancel()` run with no await between them, so the cancellation is already pending before the woken agent can run.
- **review-01 #4 and review-08's deletion suggestions (`ModelTurn.text`, `RolloutRecorder.limits`, `AgentCompletion`, `NO_TOOLS`, `_ShellToolSession.close`, double `judge_connection` call, docstring deferral):** style/API-surface preferences, not behavior the code gets wrong.
- **review-02 #1 (shell capability without a machine passes `check`):** `check_spec` rejects any non-empty environment requirements — including the shell capability — when no machine is selected (`checks.py:59-61`), so the `ValueError` in `_ShellHarness.run` is unreachable through the engine.
- **review-02 #3 (length-stop comment in `start`):** the comment explains why LENGTH is excluded from the explicit start-check; `_refusal` refuses any `start` after a length stop regardless, and the `start` docstring makes no contrary promise.
- **review-02 #5 (`command_timeout` without a default):** a deliberate API choice, not a defect; the doc example passes it explicitly.
- **review-02 #6 and review-09 #8 (`ADVANCE_INCOMPLETE` and last-step-only metrics in `Rollout.metrics`):** both are documented behavior (`task-rollouts.md:464-465`; "The last step's metrics").
- **review-03 #4 (`stop_at_turn_deadline` naming):** the tool-deadline-interrupts vs. total-timeout-stops distinction is documented (`task-rollouts.md:438`).
- **review-04 #1 (tool deadline demotes a model error):** the tool deadline is disarmed for the whole model request (`recorder.py:299`) and rearmed only on success, so `model_error` and `tool.expired()` cannot hold together when the checks run.
- **review-04 #2 (length stop leaves the tool deadline armed):** same disarm — `_send` clears the tool deadline at line 299 and the `GenerationLimitReached` branch raises before any rearm.
- **review-04 #5 (`delivery` unbound in `run_task`):** an exception inside the `try` propagates after the `finally`; the code after the `try`/`finally` never executes, so `delivery` cannot be unbound there.
- **review-05 #4 and #6 (judge capture overhead; verifier timeout covering capture and grading):** the single `verifier_timeout` covering output capture plus grading is documented in the deadlines table (`task-rollouts.md:426`); the capture-overhead point is a minor optimization.
- **review-09 #3 (old `RolloutEngine(model, factories)` order):** no in-repo caller passes the old order; an `isinstance` assertion is speculative migration aid, not a defect in this PR.
- **review-09 #4 (judge grader's `environment` ignored):** documented design — the judge grades on the host, so no machine is used for its environment (`checks.py:38-39`).
- **review-09 #5 (`record(observations=...)` then `start` allowed):** intended — the recorded observations end the earlier conversation's last step and `start` begins a new conversation, exactly as the `start` and `record` docstrings describe.
- **review-09 #7 (agent check misses provider tools):** `check` rejects every task with `tool_providers` (`agent.py:51`); only the error message names action interfaces rather than tool names.
- **review-05 #2/#3/#5, review-06 #3-#6, review-03 #2:** real but marginal polish (observation overwrite, a missing `TransitionCompleted` on the total-timeout path, empty standalone `outputs`, untested `harness_rollout` failure path/`response_end`, judge fallback key wording, `response_token_ids` mode wording) — dropped for rank, not disputed.

</details>

issues.body:
Held-out LM evaluation fails when token positions are explicitly sharded across a context mesh. Training updates succeed; the first evaluation raises:

```text
lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py:238, _default_lm_eval_loss_fn
per_pos_token_id = jnp.roll(named_batch.tokens.array, -1, axis=-1)
ShardingTypeError: `a` cannot be sharded on the axis being rolled over.
Got arr type=i32[16@(replica_dcn,data,expert),32768@context] and axis=(1,)
```

Reproduce:
1. Use an explicit mesh with local axes `data=1, replica=1, model=1, expert=8` and inter-node axes `replica_dcn=1, context=4` (32 GPUs).
2. Map `batch` to `(replica_dcn,data,expert)` and `position` to `context`, with global batch 16 and sequence length 32,768.
3. Run `cb_tagged_lm_evaluate` on a model and batch with that layout. Its default loss callback reaches the failing roll.

Expected: target-token shifting and token-weighted evaluation agree with an unsharded reference. The training loss path in `models/loss.py` already gathers the token IDs along the sharded position axis before shifting and restores their layout afterward.

Observed in the #10213 sweep at completed update 548, its first held-out evaluation, on base commit `753bbb163c78f0e7ea50059522f42156708162c8` plus experiment-local changes. Iris job: `/karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft`. Retrieve the error with `uv run iris --cluster=marin task logs /karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft/1 --substring ShardingTypeError`.

The labeled callback contains the same roll at `eval.py:277`; that path was not exercised in this run. This issue tracks the shared evaluator fix separately from moving the sweep's validation offline.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Both default LM evaluation callbacks call `jnp.roll` on token arrays whose position axis may be explicitly sharded. JAX rejects that roll before the evaluator can aggregate loss or byte counts. The evaluator already receives the mesh mapping needed to restore the token layout after shifting.

**Relevant code**
- [`eval.py#L223-L237`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L223-L237) — tagged callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L259-L276`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L259-L276) — labeled callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L531-L577`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L531-L577) — token IDs feed byte aggregation

# Proposed Fix

`TaggedEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` or `LabeledEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` → default loss callback → `jnp.roll` on context-sharded positions → `ShardingTypeError`. Replicate the position axis for the shift, then restore its mapped sharding in both default callbacks; verify token IDs and token-weighted metrics against an unsharded reference on a small context mesh.

The full Levanter run hit an unrelated Grug MoE test that uses `ragged-all-to-all`, which XLA:CPU does not support; all-files Pyrefly reported missing optional imports outside the changed files.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Design stage, 2026-10-16. We compare five supervised fine-tuning (SFT) mechanisms for agentic coding on one base, one task pool, one teacher and one supervised-token budget: plain SFT (one accepted demonstration per task), rejection-sampled SFT with resampling across epochs, relay SFT (#10027), recovery SFT, and plateau dropping (#10028). The earlier transfer experiments (#9920, #9984) compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT, on-policy distillation and weight merging on non-agentic tasks; this experiment moves to agentic tasks under the eval policy (#10197) and drops merging and distillation. Nothing has trained yet except a learning-rate sweep of the control, which is in progress.

## Question

Which mechanism, if any, improves Snowball v0 on SWE-bench Verified and the terminal benchmarks over plain SFT at equal supervised tokens, without losing retention on GSM8K, BFCL-Parity and GPQA-Diamond.

## Fixed choices

- Base: Snowball v0 = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12` @ `4eeb756b`. v0 carries a diluted DARE graft of the allkimi relay SFT, so relay's lift reads smaller than it would on a pre-graft checkpoint; this is accepted because the question is what improves the release.
- Task pool: about 2,200 TMax environments (`allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K`, tasks.zip) and about 2,100 SWE-smith tasks sampled from the Harbor packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`, stratified by repository, SWE-bench Verified repositories removed, decontaminated through DataKit against SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite 2.0. Selection is outcome-blind. SWE-smith packages receive a git-history strip before the agent phase (#10212).
- Harness per task family, matching the policy's scoring agent: TMax under Terminus-2, SWE-smith under mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, both in Harbor under the policy pins.
- Teacher: GLM 5.3 through the internal inference service, 8 attempts per task, verified by each task's tests. v0 is never sampled except in relay, where it starts each task and GLM continues after a trigger (format error, context budget, completion claim).
- Recipe, shared by every arm: the #9984 comparison-arm settings (AdamW, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, clip 1.0, router bias frozen, batch 16 at 32k context, constant learning rate, loss averaged over supervised tokens), 3 epochs, replay of general SFT data (`nemotron_sft_v3`, reasoning kept) at one quarter of the agentic budget. The learning rate comes from the sweep below.

## Arms and token matching

B is the supervised-token count of the plain arm: the first passing attempt per task with at least one pass, one trajectory per task. Every arm trains on B agentic tokens plus the same replay slice for the same number of optimizer steps.

- Plain SFT (control): as above.
- RS-multi: identical task slots to plain; when a task recurs in a later epoch, a different passing attempt is used. Measures demonstration diversity at a fixed budget.
- Relay (#10027): v0's own turns stay in context with no loss; GLM's turns are trained; passing episodes subsampled to B. Episodes with no teacher turn are dropped.
- Recovery (phase 2): the plain trajectories; 20% receive one or two synthetic failed turns re-rendered in v0's measured error styles plus the real harness error, inserted through the parser; injections carry no loss, so the budget equals B by construction. Waits on a validated injection generator.
- Plateau dropping (#10028, phase 2): the plain trajectories; tokens whose loss has plateaued lose gradient; matched on optimizer steps, with gradient-carrying tokens reported. Waits on the trainer.

Phase 1 is plain, RS-multi and relay.

## Evaluation

Every arm, including plain, runs the retention gate (GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, GPQA-Diamond) and the agentic endpoint (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, TBLite 2.0) under the policy's trial counts and pins. An arm passes when it has no decisive loss against plain on the gate and a decisive win over plain on at least one agentic benchmark with no decisive loss on the others, where decisive is the policy's rule (gap above 1.96 times the combined task-level standard error, each scaled by 1/sqrt(0.9)). One policy run resolves gaps of roughly 4 to 5 points on SWE-bench Verified and 8 to 10 on the terminal benchmarks; unresolved arms are reported with intervals and not promoted. Passing arms, plain and v0 go to the 23-benchmark tournament.

## Learning-rate sweep of the control

Running now, on pilot data (existing Qwen3.6-27B TMax traces and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces, history-reading trials removed), four runs from v0 at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5, 3 epochs, recipe otherwise fixed. Screens per run: held-out validation loss on 5% of tasks, GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified random-100 and a 100-task TBLite subset. Decision rule, fixed in advance: among rates with no decisive retention loss against v0, the best equal-weight mean of the two agentic screens; ties to the smaller rate. The chosen rate is confirmed once on the real plain-arm data and then frozen for all arms.

## Budget

Core (sweep, generation, phase 1, tournament) about 3,700 to 4,000 H100-hours; phase 2 adds about 2,400, of which 1,700 is an optional 20-epoch plateau comparison. GLM generation runs on the internal service and sandbox CPU and is outside the GPU budget.

## Status and next steps

- Pilot dataset and learning-rate sweep: in progress.
- Task pool, decontamination and package fix: in progress.
- Harness bring-up, one-task dry runs, a 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilot and a relay dry run: in progress. The full 8-attempt generation waits on their results.
- Then: phase-1 training, first-stage evaluation, tournament for passers; phase 2 when its code exists.

Design notes and diagrams are kept in the maintainer's notes and will be attached as results land.

## Decision log

- 2026-10-15: scope cut to SFT only; merging and on-policy distillation dropped. Base set to Snowball v0.
- 2026-10-16: one harness per task family following the policy's scoring agents; GLM 5.3 as the single teacher with regenerated traces instead of reusing Kimi and Qwen traces; RS arm redefined as resampling across epochs after the token-budgeted variant was found to re-weight tasks; task eligibility defined by teacher success only; unfiltered-SFT control dropped; primary endpoint set to the agentic benchmarks with the tournament secondary; git-history leak found in the SWE-smith packages and a strip added to the pool build.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

No shootout arm has trained on the new task pool; the learning-rate sweep, package repair, and harness pilots are still in progress. Two checks are essential before full generation: [#10212](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212) documents a SWE-smith git-history leak, and [#10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) preserves relay turn flags but does not yet apply the teacher-only loss mask.

**Relevant code**
- [`launcher.py#L554-L564`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/sft/launcher.py#L554-L564) — chat SFT masks user turns.
- [`datasets.py#L477-L493`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L477-L493) — assistant spans receive loss.

# Proposed Fix

1. Validate the repaired SWE-smith packages from #10212: no agent-visible history or branches, gold patch passes, and unpatched task fails. Freeze an outcome-blind, decontaminated task manifest and report excluded history-reading traces.
2. Finish one-task dry runs, the 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilots, and a relay dry run under the pinned harnesses. Verify that relay student turns have zero loss after rendering while teacher turns retain loss. Start eight-attempt GLM generation only after those checks pass.
3. Finish the learning-rate sweep and confirm its selected rate on real plain-arm data. Give plain and RS-multi identical task slots, subsample relay to B supervised agentic tokens, and match all three arms on B, one-quarter replay, and optimizer steps; publish the token counts, manifests, checkpoints, and run links.
4. Evaluate phase 1 under [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197), publish task-level scores and uncertainty for the retention gate and three agentic endpoints, and send only passing arms to the tournament. Run recovery and plateau dropping after validating the injection mask and trainer; report inconclusive arms with intervals instead of promoting them.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Teacher generation bring-up: one-task dry runs

## TL;DR

GLM 5.3 now runs end to end in both harnesses (Harbor `016dd78b`, Daytona sandboxes, run from cw-us-east-02a):
- TMax under Terminus-2, with the 65,536 / 16,384 limits from the policy;
- SWE-smith under the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter, with a 32,768-token window.

**The adapter question is answered.** The mini-swe-agent adapter runs a raw SWE-smith Harbor package unchanged, and the dry-run trace fit inside 32k (largest prompt 13.4k tokens). One trace says nothing about the length distribution; the pilot will measure it.

**The GLM pass on SWE-smith read the fix from git history** (#10212). Before the SWE-smith pass-rate pilot, the packages need the history-stripped repair.

**The pilot has not started.** It waits on a capacity confirmation for the GLM service.

## Per trial

| | TMax `task_000000_5c5b0938` | SWE-smith `swesmith-00003` |
|---|---|---|
| Reward | 0 in the first run, 1 in a rerun | 1 in both runs |
| Model calls | 4 | 16 to 17 |
| Prompt tokens (total / largest) | 9.3k to 10.1k / 3.7k | 145k to 156k (about 93% prefix-cached) / 13.4k |
| Completion tokens (reasoning) | 5.1k to 6.2k (4.2k to 5.2k) | 3.4k to 3.6k (0.5k to 0.8k) |
| Model time | 39 s | 16 s |
| Trial wall time | 42 to 93 s (environment build 3 to 45 s) | 74 to 80 s (verifier 20 to 25 s) |

## Effective generation settings

Both clients send only `model` and `max_tokens=16384`, so GLM runs on the service defaults. GLM 5.3's template then renders `Reasoning Effort: Max`.

Every request is logged by an in-cluster proxy. The log records the settings as sent and the full reply, reasoning included. The proxy also serves `/tokenize` with the `zai-org/GLM-5.3` tokenizer, because the mini-swe-agent context limiter needs it and the relay does not provide it. Its token counts matched the service on every request.

## Transcripts

Both harnesses write Harbor ATIF trajectories:
- **Terminus-2:** each step's message is the JSON action, and the reasoning is in `reasoning_content`.
- **mini-swe-agent:** native `bash` tool calls with `{returncode, output}` observations, but the trajectory **drops GLM's reasoning**. Training rows are therefore rebuilt from the proxy log, which keeps it. That rebuild checks clean on both dry runs.

## What the agent can see

Measured with an oracle-agent probe during the agent phase:

| | TMax (converted) | SWE-smith (raw package) |
|---|---|---|
| `/tests` | absent | absent |
| `/solution` | absent | absent |
| Other task files | none | none |
| Git history | no repository | 944 branches, including `main` and the full history |

The SWE-smith dry-run pass used that history: it ran `git show 614b134:<file>`, then checked its edit against that file. Details are in #10212.

## Other findings

- **TMax is not in Harbor format** in `tasks.zip`. The pool converts it with TMax's own `convert_to_harbor.py` at `hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`, minus 181 environments with hidden verifier assets, giving 2,019 tasks.
- **The dry-run TMax task looks flawed.** It runs an OpenMP parallel loop over the outer LU loop with 4 threads, while the test expects the sequential determinant. The task failed once and passed once.

## Next

- **TMax pilot:** 200 tasks x 2 attempts, seed 20261016, drawn uniformly from 1,963 eligible tasks (the pool minus #202's held-out ids). Staged; starts when capacity is confirmed.
- **SWE-smith pilot:** 200 x 2, stratified by repository, on the history-stripped packages.
- **Relay dry run:** 20 tasks per family, with v0 served by the policy serving config. GLM takes over on these triggers:
  - format error: GLM writes one repair turn;
  - context budget at 0.75 of the window: GLM continues to the end;
  - completion claim: v0's reply is withheld and logged, and GLM continues to the end.

Run folders: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/{tmax-dry1,tmax-dry2,swe-dry3,swe-dry4,visibility1}`

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
Native crates currently live under their owning Python packages, including `lib/finelog/rust`, `lib/dupekit/rust`, and `lib/iris/rust`. The layout keeps each wheel isolated, but it does not provide a Cargo workspace for shared internal crates, dependency versions, build profiles, lint policy, or release tooling.

Define whether Marin should use a top-level `rust/` workspace with reusable internal crates and thin PyO3 extension crates that remain independently buildable and publishable. The design should preserve Python package ownership and dependency direction; changing one native component must not require publishing every native wheel.

Done when:
- A design records the workspace layout, crate ownership rules, dependency boundaries, lockfile policy, and versioning model.
- A prototype shows two PyO3 extensions sharing an internal Rust crate while building and publishing as separate Python distributions.
- CI runs shared formatting, lint, and tests, then builds only affected wheels.
- Local `uv` development and Docker builds remain reproducible without requiring a prior PyPI release.
- The migration plan covers the existing finelog, dupekit, and Iris native crates.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan (design task — analysis for human review, no PR):**
- [x] Read AGENTS + fix-issue/commit skills
- [x] Actionability check
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PRs/issues)
- [x] Survey current native-crate layout, CI, release, dev flow
- [x] Post research + proposed approach

# Research

Actionable but scoped as **design + prototype**, not a code fix — the "Done when" list needs a design doc, a two-extension prototype, CI changes, and a migration plan (>100 LOC). Following the task rules I'm posting analysis, not a PR.

Current state — **two independent Cargo workspaces, no shared crates, no `lib/iris/rust`** (the issue's premise is off here: Iris has no native crate; it only *consumes* the `finelog_server` module — [`log_stack.py#L84`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/log_stack.py#L84)):

- [`lib/finelog/rust/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/Cargo.toml) — workspace: `finelog` lib + `finelog-server` bin + `pyext` cdylib (`marin-finelog-server`). Pins **arrow/parquet 58**, **pyo3 0.29**, `datafusion 53`; profiles `release`/`fast`.
- [`lib/dupekit/rust/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/dupekit/rust/Cargo.toml) — single crate `dupekit-native`. Pins **arrow/parquet 57.1**, **pyo3 0.26**; profile `release` only.
- Separate `Cargo.lock` per tree; the uv workspace **excludes** both ([`pyproject.toml#L143-L149`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/pyproject.toml#L149)); dev source-builds via `scripts/rust_mode.py`.
- Independent publish: [`dupekit-release-wheels.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/dupekit-release-wheels.yaml), [`finelog-release-wheels.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/finelog-release-wheels.yaml); per-crate CI with paths-filter ([`rust-checks.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/rust-checks.yaml)).

**Root tension:** the two crates share *no code today*, so a workspace's payoff is shared dep pins, lint/profile policy, release tooling, and a home for *future* shared crates. The cost is that one Cargo workspace resolves **one** version of each dep through a single lockfile — so arrow (57.1 vs 58) and pyo3 (0.26 vs 0.29) must be unified first. That unification is the real prerequisite, independent of the layout.

# Proposed Approach

Adopt a top-level **virtual** workspace `rust/` (`[workspace]` with members, no root package) that owns policy but keeps each PyO3 extension a thin, independently-buildable crate. Publishing stays per-wheel: maturin already targets each ext via `manifest-path`, so a single lockfile does **not** couple releases. Wheels only rebuild when their paths change (paths-filter already models this).

Layout sketch:

```
rust/
  Cargo.toml            # [workspace] members + [workspace.dependencies] + [workspace.lints] + [profile.*]
  Cargo.lock            # single lockfile
  crates/
    finelog/            # lib + finelog-server bin  (was lib/finelog/rust)
    finelog-pyext/      # cdylib -> marin-finelog-server
    dupekit-native/     # cdylib -> marin-dupekit    (was lib/dupekit/rust)
    shared-*/           # e.g. arrow<->pyarrow FFI or hashing helpers
```

Decisions a human should settle before implementation:
1. **Move crates into `rust/` vs. keep them under `lib/*` and add a virtual root** that path-references them. Moving is cleaner but churns maturin `manifest-path`, uv `[tool.uv.sources]`, `rust_mode.py`, cache-keys, and both release workflows. Keeping-in-place minimizes churn but scatters the tree.
2. **Dependency unification cost/timing** — bump dupekit to arrow 58 / pyo3 0.26→0.29 (behavioral: pyo3 0.26→0.29 has API changes). This is the gating work.
3. **Shared-crate for the prototype** — smallest real candidate that two exts can share (arrow↔pyarrow conversion or a hashing wrapper), to satisfy the "two extensions sharing an internal crate" criterion without inventing indirection.
4. **Lockfile policy** — single committed `rust/Cargo.lock`; update the `rust_mode.py`/CI dev-mode leak guard and `Swatinem/rust-cache` `workspaces:` paths accordingly.

Recommend a `.agents/projects/` design doc plus a minimal prototype PR (shared crate + one converted ext) rather than a big-bang migration. I can draft the design doc next if you want to proceed.

comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖 Proposal is up for review: consolidate the native crates into a shared Rust workspace.

PR: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7569 — design doc at `.agents/projects/2026-07-23_rust_workspace_consolidation.md`.

The shape: one top-level `rust/` workspace holding `rust/crates/*` internal libraries (`publish = false`, path-only, never on crates.io) and thin `rust/<pkg>-pyext` cdylibs that each build one wheel. Wheel names, module names, and public APIs stay the same. The first shared crate is the auth/JWT verify that finelog (`auth.rs`, 1053 lines) and iris (`auth.rs`, 541 lines) duplicate today and that rigging can reuse. One committed `rust/Cargo.lock`, with `[workspace.dependencies]` and a `cargo-deny` singleton policy doing the actual version unification (a single lock alone does not force one arrow/pyo3 — that took a review round to get right), plus a new cargo dependabot entry.

I built the prototype (cargo 1.97.1 / maturin 1.14.1) rather than assert the mechanic: two extensions sharing an internal crate build as separate wheels at independent versions from one workspace/lock, and each sdist vendors the shared crate (maturin prunes the workspace manifest to just that wheel's crates) and builds standalone under `--locked` with no surrounding workspace and no prior release of the shared crate. A second pass covered the real `pyext → component → internal` finelog shape and reproduced a Docker failure — a context copying a subset of workspace members fails at load, so Docker copies the whole `rust/` tree. Output is in the doc.

A codex review hardened it: the single-lock fix above; crate boundaries need a `cargo metadata` graph check since cargo only enforces cycle-freedom and pyo3's `links` singleness; pyo3 unifies first (dupekit 0.26→0.29) as its own PR before a mechanical `git mv` that retargets every build consumer atomically; and the shared-JWT extraction is gated on a behavior matrix plus regression suite.

On growing iris into Rust (your follow-up), the doc has a "Future direction" section. Feasible, and the workspace helps: move compute kernels with narrow interfaces (reconcile diff, scheduler core, token verify, RPC hot paths) and keep the churny multi-system glue in Python, so the dataplane/control-plane seam stays. finelog already proves one component lib can be both a binary and a PyO3 extension, so iris can grow an `iris-core` consumed in-process and/or over RPC from one crate graph; the risk to manage is FFI-surface sprawl.

Open questions for you:
1. Home for the shared auth crate — `rust/crates/marin-jwt`, or an `auth` crate with `jwt` as one module, since iris's IAP/session/federation surface is larger than finelog's?
2. Rigging reuse — a PyO3 wheel on the shared auth crate, or rigging calls finelog/iris's existing extension? This is the one question that changes the crate taxonomy.
3. arrow/parquet order — keep the finelog 58 / dupekit 57.1 split (allowlisted) through the move and bump dupekit separately, or bump up front?
4. Platform owner for `rust/crates/**` in CODEOWNERS.

I can start the rollout at Phase 1a (the pyo3 unification) on your go, or adjust the layout first.

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
Try **per-head MuonH** on the MLA kv-latent up-projections: orthogonalize each head's `(kv_lora, head_dim)` block independently instead of the full `(kv_lora, n·head_dim)` matrix. Per `experiments/grug/moe/ablation_runbook.md`.

**Branch:** https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/grug/moe-abl/per-head-muon-kv

## Verbatim prompt

> lets follow ablation doc and make a new issue. lets try per head muon, where the projections from kv_latent -> k and v have muon applied seperately per head. this way, the projection from 512->1024 is replaced with 512->128. lets also run at d2048, where we replace 512->2048 with 512->128. only apply the change to the K and V projections. Leave Q as is. Apply in whichever way is simplest: custom reshape in optimizer, or storing parameters in stacked shape. This should be 2 runs, one for each size.

## Change under test

`w_uk` (kv_latent → k_nope) and `w_uv` (kv_latent → v) are `(kv_lora=512, n·head_dim)`. Muon currently Newton-Schulzes them as one matrix. This ablation orthogonalizes **each head's `(512, 128)` block separately** — so the `512→n·128` projection becomes `n` independent `512→128` orthogonalizations:
- **d1024**: n=8 → `512→1024` becomes 8× `512→128`.
- **d2048**: n=16 → `512→2048` becomes 16× `512→128`.

**Only K and V** (`w_uk`, `w_uv`). **Q (`w_uq`) is unchanged** (full-matrix Muon).

Implementation (simplest = **custom reshape in the optimizer**): `SCALE_MUON_PER_HEAD_KV=1` makes `grugmuon`'s `transform_array` split the trailing `n·128` axis of `w_uk`/`w_uv`, vmap the replicated NS over the (head, scan-layer) batch, and reshape back. No model/forward/sharding change, so scan stays on and the runs are directly comparable to the `mla-base` LR-sweep points. spillover_issues.author: weaverbot
spillover_issues.body:
## Description

The opencode RL "literal log" — how a CLI agent's per-token training signal (`token_ids`/`logprobs`/`chat_history`) is recovered for TIS — is today a single append-only JSONL file (10s of MB) written by the harbor RecordProxy and read by MarinSkyRL's `TerminalBenchGenerator`. Both sides hand-roll the framing independently:

- **writer** (harbor/otagent): appends newline-delimited JSON to one shared, growing, worker-local file.
- **reader** (MarinSkyRL): incremental byte-offset reads, partial-line carry, inode/shrink rotation detection, and a hand-built `{trial_id: [entries]}` index (see `LiteralLogStore` in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#49).

This is fragile (no corruption detection, partial records, rotation edge cases) and is an anti-pattern on object storage: a single mutable file appended-while-read maps badly onto GCS/S3 — no efficient append, no tailing an open object, eventual consistency.

Replace the ad-hoc JSONL-file contract with **one consolidated reader/writer interface** — a shared library used by BOTH sides — that owns the record schema, framing, coordination, and per-trial indexing, and is object-storage-native. Cross-repo cleanup: the writer lives in harbor/otagent (here), the reader in MarinSkyRL, so the shared interface belongs in this repo and both depend on it.

### Definition of Done

- A shared LogStore module (writer + reader) with a single defined record schema + framing, replacing the JSONL-file contract — neither side hand-rolls parsing or indexing.
- **Object-storage-native layout**: immutable *sealed segments + a manifest* (list-a-prefix, read-sealed-objects), not one mutable growing file. Works on local FS **and** `gs://` without the append-while-read hazard. This rules out SQLite/WAL (needs local POSIX locking) and single-file Parquet (can't tail a half-written file) — see the format analysis in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#49.
- Smarter than 10s-of-MB of JSON: at minimum length-framed + CRC'd records (corruption detection); columnar/compressed sealed segments (Arrow IPC or Parquet-per-segment) where scan efficiency is wanted.
- Per-trial lookup + write/read coordination are library features, tested once.
- harbor RecordProxy writes via it; MarinSkyRL's `LiteralLogStore` is replaced by (or thinly wraps) the shared reader, with a **dual-read compatibility window** (reader accepts old JSONL + new segments during rollout, since the two sides ship in separately-built images).

Refs: marin-community/MarinSkyRL#49 (`LiteralLogStore` + format-migration analysis), marin-community/MarinSkyRL#51 (e2e gate that would exercise it), marin-community/MarinSkyRL#37 / #38 / #41.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + confirm actionability
- [x] Locate the writer (harbor RecordProxy) and reader (MarinSkyRL `LiteralLogStore`) in this repo
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues)
- [x] Post research + proposed approach

# Research

The design goal (object-storage-native manifest + sealed-segment LogStore replacing the append-while-read JSONL contract) is well-specified with a concrete DoD, so it's actionable — but it's a **large, cross-repo design change**, not a self-contained bug fix, so this is an analysis comment for human review, not a PR.

Blocking scope finding: **neither endpoint the issue names exists in `marin-community/marin`.** No `RecordProxy`, `LiteralLogStore`, `otagent`, `opencode`, or literal-log JSONL code is present. The writer lives in harbor/OT-Agent and the reader in `MarinSkyRL` (`#49`) — both separate repos. What *is* here:

- `harbor_evaluator.py` — only a CLI wrapper around `harbor run` that parses trial JSON; it does not read/write the literal log.
- PR #7246 (`feuer/agentic-evals-extraction`) extracts agentic-evals infra *out of* OT-Agent into `experiments/agentic_evals/` (presets/serve/harness/runtime/results/backends) — and pointedly does **not** include the RecordProxy / literal-log writer.

So before any implementation: **where does the shared library live, given the writer and reader are built into separately-shipped images in two other repos?** That ownership decision is a prerequisite and belongs to a human.

**Relevant code / prior art**
- [`rollout_storage.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/rollout_storage.py) — already the exact pattern the issue asks for: a `create_reader()/create_writer()` config interface with `FileRolloutReader`/`FileRolloutWriter` writing **one immutable file per batch over fsspec** (glob-a-prefix, read-sealed-files, no append-while-read). Object-storage-native; works on local FS and `gs://`.
- [`harbor_evaluator.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/harbor_evaluator.py) — the only harbor surface in-repo (CLI wrapper, not the log path).
- PR #7246 — OT-Agent extraction; the natural in-repo home for a writer, but currently excludes it.

# Proposed approach

Follow the `rollout_storage.py` model rather than inventing a new format layer — it already solves the append-while-read hazard the issue calls out.

- **Layout**: writer emits immutable sealed segments under a per-run prefix (`<prefix>/<worker>/<seq>.arrow`) plus a `manifest.json`; reader lists the prefix and reads sealed objects. No mutable growing file, so GCS eventual consistency and lack of append/tailing are non-issues.
- **Records**: length-framed + CRC32C per record for corruption detection; segment payload as Arrow IPC (columnar, compressed, scan-efficient) — rules out SQLite/WAL (POSIX locking) and single-file Parquet (can't tail a half-written file), matching the `#49` analysis.
- **Per-trial index**: `{trial_id: [(segment, row_range)]}` built from the manifest, a library feature tested once — deletes the reader's hand-rolled byte-offset/inode/shrink-rotation logic.
- **Dual-read window**: reader accepts legacy JSONL *and* new segments during rollout (the two sides ship in separate images).
- **Home**: put the shared lib where both sides can depend on it. Given the writer's in-repo landing spot is #7246's `experiments/agentic_evals/`, and the closest reusable code is `lib/marin/.../rl/rollout_storage.py`, a small `logstore` module under `lib/` that #7246 and MarinSkyRL both import is the least-duplicating option — but this needs sign-off since it creates a new cross-repo dependency.

Recommend a human confirm the ownership/home question and whether to generalize `rollout_storage.py` vs. add a sibling `logstore` before implementation starts.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
_Filed by an AI agent on behalf of **@penfever** (LAION / OpenThoughts), labeled `agent-generated` per the repo's [AI-generated contributions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/dev-guide/contributing.md) policy._

@rjpower — do you think we could surface some summary stats from **Iris finelog** that would let us track Marin **preemptible compute use weekly**, drop it into **MWS** as a summary section, and map it to **users** (certainly) and ideally to **public GitHub issues**? I think it would give everyone greater confidence about "where the compute is all going."

The motivation is transparency. "Where did the compute go this week?" currently gets answered anecdotally. A weekly, per-user (and ideally per-issue) rollup of preemptible TPU-hours — plus how much we lose to preemption churn — would give the team one shared, citable picture instead.

### Why this looks tractable today

Iris already carries most of the raw material:

- **Attribution is first-class.** Jobs carry `owner_principal` / `submitting_user` (controller.proto), and there's a `ListUsers` API — so per-user rollups don't need to parse names out of job paths.
- **Per-job compute + waste is already derivable from finelog job history.** `scripts/iris/analyze_job_history.py` paginates the full history and reports `total_runtime_s`, `iris_preemption_count`, per-cycle placement/serve, etc. Aggregate that across a week by user × cluster × accelerator and you get chip-hours plus a preemption-overhead figure.
- **Region / accelerator are on the placement**, so we can split v5p vs v6e and us-central1 vs us-east5 vs europe-west4.

### Proposed shape

1. A weekly job that reads finelog (or reuses the `analyze_job_history` aggregation) and emits, per ISO week:
   - preemptible TPU **chip-hours** by **user**, by **cluster/region**, by **accelerator type**;
   - a **preemption-overhead** metric — chip-hours (or wall-time) lost to preempt → re-place churn vs. productive compute. This is the "what are we actually paying for preemptible" number, and it's the one people are surprised by;
   - top-N jobs by chip-hours.
2. Drop a compact table into **MWS** each week (the same weekly-summary artifact the team already reads), so it shows up where people are already looking.
3. **Stretch — map to GitHub issues.** This is the one piece of glue that doesn't exist cleanly today. Users are easy (`owner_principal`); issues need a job → issue link — e.g. a launch-time convention (`issue=#NNNN` in job labels/metadata) or a maintained lookup. Worth deciding whether that's in scope for v1 or a follow-up.

### Open questions

- **Finelog retention** — is a full ISO-week of job/task events reliably inside the retention window, or do we need to snapshot the weekly aggregate before it ages out? (This probably decides whether the weekly job is "read finelog directly" vs. "roll up incrementally into a durable table.")
- **Preemptible vs. reserved** — preemptible-only, or report both with a split?
- **"Productive vs. wasted" definition** — do cold-compile / resume-scan chip-hours count as overhead, or only the re-placement gaps between attempts?
- **Attribution granularity** — user-level for v1 with issue-level as a fast-follow, or hold for the issue link?

Happy to prototype the finelog → weekly-aggregate step if the shape sounds right — the per-job pieces are already there in `analyze_job_history`; the new parts are the weekly grouping, the overhead metric, and the MWS drop.

🤖 Scoped and published as a design PR: #7387 (`design.md` / `research.md` / `spec.md` under `.agents/projects/iris_compute_accounting/`). Ran the codex peer review you asked for, plus a fable and an architect pass — they found two load-bearing things that reshaped the doc.

**On your "iris event `<started/preempted/resumed/finished> <user> <time> <resources>`" intuition** — that's exactly the missing piece and it's the core of the proposal: a durable `iris.accounting` finelog namespace, one row per terminated attempt. The catch the review surfaced is that it **must be captured at terminalization inside the controller**, not read back weekly. Zone/region/preemptible live on the `workers` row, and `remove_worker` deletes that row and NULLs `task_attempts.worker_id` in the *same transaction* that terminalizes a preempted attempt (`writes.py:734`) — so a post-hoc query sees NULL placement for the entire preemption cohort at t=0, and `worker_retention` is only 24h anyway. (`iris.task_event` is a same-named red herring: k8s scheduling verdicts, ~1h retention.) So there's no "just query finelog weekly" shortcut for the preemptible split — the emit is the work.

**On prometheus MFU** — good news: MFU-per-job is *already* durable in the finelog `telltale` namespace (`levanter_throughput_mfu`), and Grafana already reads it. Two caveats: it's Levanter-training-only (vLLM/Zephyr emit nothing), and TPUs have **no** hardware duty-cycle telemetry at all, so for TPUs MFU is the only "are the chips busy" signal. "Downtime" needs the same terminalization capture (recovery-idle = gap between a preempted attempt finishing and the next starting).

**One honesty flag on the headline number:** "chip-hours lost to preemption" as full preempted-attempt runtime is a large over-count — Levanter checkpoints and resumes, and user cancels land as KILLED-with-started rows. The doc reports a labeled *upper bound* plus a separately-computed recovery-idle figure instead.

```sql
  WHERE name='levanter_throughput_mfu' AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}}
  GROUP BY job_id, run, ts)
SELECT job_id, run, round(avg(mfu),1) AS mean_mfu, count(*) steps
FROM per_step GROUP BY job_id, run ORDER BY steps DESC;
```

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment evaluated whether TransformerEngine NCCL_EP could replace or beat Marin's incumbent `a2a_cute` expert-parallel MoE path on GB200/B200 systems. The core goal was met: TE/NCCL_EP builds, imports, and trains at 64 GPUs with EP8, with loss parity and near-parity throughput. A custom NCCL_EP transport seam plus MoE-layer chunking made the production b1024 x seq4096 d5120 L48 case train at 18.0% MFU versus 19.1% for `a2a_cute`, and chunk rematerialization removed the no-drop EP capacity wall by making peak EP memory scale with one chunk rather than full batch/seqlen. The later fairness and gap-closing work found that TE's full `moe()` block performs about the same as the custom seam but remains around 1.1-1.3 percentage points behind `a2a_cute`; command-buffer scoping, collective-overlap flags, and `max_num_sms` tuning were wash-or-loss in bf16. The current recommendation is to keep `a2a_cute` as the incumbent for bf16, preserve NCCL_EP/chunking as a derisked path, and next pursue NVIDIA/TE follow-ups: report the TE main-tip 64-GPU regression, test quantized fp8/MXFP8 support when available, and revisit NGC-stack arms after the compile stall is understood.

### Helpful links
- Full logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md
- 64-GPU EP8 goal gate: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5008121573
- Production b1024 chunking result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5009585521
- Full TE MoE block benchmark: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5073227834
- Gap-closing benchmark and TE tip regression: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5076118699
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

NVIDIA's recommendations for EP MoE on JAX/XLA GPU (2026-07-13/14):

1. `jax.ragged_dot` was made performant in NGC JAX 26.05 (`xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion=ON`, confirmed supported on B200).
2. TransformerEngine has a MoE block backed by NCCL_EP ([TE #3036](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3036), C API in [TE #3034](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3034)) — "equivalent to DeepEP/HybridEP with no external dependency". The 8k-seq-len staging limit (which caps local batch size at 2) is actively being removed.
3. The JAX MoE speed-of-light solution will require TransformerEngine as the time-to-market way to expose NCCL_EP.

The full TE MoE block (router/permute, hybridEP A2A, grouped GEMMs) lives on the WIP branch [`jberchtold/teddy-te-ep-integration-2026-07-08-support-quantization`](https://github.com/jberchtold-nvidia/TransformerEngine/blob/jberchtold/teddy-te-ep-integration-2026-07-08-support-quantization/transformer_engine/jax/moe.py), targeted for merge into TE main. Early external testing of that branch is reportedly promising.

Prior state on our side (#7012 / #7279): hypothesis H-te is Blocked in the [7012 logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7012-b200-mfu/.agents/logbooks/7012-b200-moe-mfu.md) — a 2026-07-15 API probe found TE 2.15.0+42b840051 ships `grouped_dense`/`permutation`/`router` but no NCCL_EP JAX surface. A source read of the TE PRs noted: 8192-token `max_tokens_per_rank` staging default, bf16-only dispatch wire (fp8 wire on the quantization WIP branch), one-sided `max_num_sms`, process-per-GPU requirement, and that it disables NCCL comm-splitting and command-buffer capture. #7279's hypothesis queue already ranks the NCCL_EP-style chunked-pipeline decomposition #1 by expected value.

## Hypothesis or Goal

NCCL_EP's SM-capped persistent comm kernels feeding chunked expert GEMMs beat our current EP legs in the latency-bound NVL72 regime. Concretely:

1. Build TE from the WIP branch on the B200 container stack and get the JAX MoE block importable.
2. Microbench dispatch/combine vs our measured baselines: XLA `ragged_all_to_all` one-shot kernel pathology (~297 ms/call, B200MFU-018) and the NCCL fallback (one-shot kernel disabled, B200MFU-025).
3. If the microbench wins, e2e MFU comparison at the canonical d2560 MoE config vs the current best (ring_cute EP4, 20.83% at 64 GPUs, #7279).
4. Assess the fp8/MXFP8 dispatch-wire path as the follow-on (dispatch bytes halve; ties into the MXFP8 work in #7282).

Caveat from prior evidence: SM-capping alone was falsified twice on this stack (B200MFU-016, B200MFU-021) — the value, if any, is in the chunked-pipeline decomposition and the fused dispatch, not the SM budget.

## Status

Goal met for build/import/train and production-shape derisking. NCCL_EP is not currently recommended as the bf16 default over `a2a_cute`: the best TE-backed arms remain about 1.3 percentage points behind `a2a_cute`, and the latest TE main tip regresses at the full 64-GPU data8 x expert8 topology. Next steps are NVIDIA escalation for that regression, quantized fp8/MXFP8 wire when TE exposes it, and NGC-stack retests after the compile stall is understood.

## Links

* Logbook: [.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md) (branch `research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep`)

* Important updates: prior context in #7012 (H-te) and #7279 (hypothesis queue)
